topic: @Transactional boundary that silently swallowed a refund
question: Riley Okonkwo has a Harbor Bike Co refund that returned 200 from refund-service — same Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.5.5 modular monolith as payment-service — but the ledger never moved and the payment is still COMPLETED. Someone caught an exception inside the @Transactional method and logged it. Explain the transaction boundary, why the refund was silently swallowed, and how you would fix it without a heroic double-write.
followUps: What happens if the same class calls this.refund() instead of going through the proxy?
Checked versus unchecked exceptions and rollback rules?
expectedConcepts: Spring rolls back on unchecked exceptions that leave the proxy
Swallowed exceptions cause commit of a partial/no-op success
Self-invocation skips @Transactional
Ledger and refund row must share one boundary
engineerAnswer: If you catch the exception inside @Transactional and return normally, Spring commits. The API can look successful while the ledger write never happened. I would let the exception propagate.
seniorAnswer: RefundApplicationService should be the boundary, not the controller. PaymentPosting or ledger work must join that transaction. If a catch block logs and returns, Spring sees a clean method and commits whatever was flushed — or commits nothing useful and still returns 200. Self-invocation of a @Transactional helper does nothing. I fix by failing the request, marking rollback, and letting the client retry with the same idempotency key. I do not add a second 'compensate' write from the catch block.
staffAnswer: I want a test that throws after the refund row save and asserts no commit and no 200. I review rollbackFor if someone used a checked exception. I look for @Transactional on private methods and for REQUIRES_NEW that committed the refund row while the ledger failed. I will not 'fix' it by bouncing a task. I will not tell Priya this is a GC event. I add a metric for refund_commit_failed and a reconciliation query, but the code fix is the boundary.
principalAnswer: A 200 with a missing ledger line is a money defect. The standard is one transaction, exceptions leave the proxy, idempotent retry. I will not accept a catch-and-return as 'resilience.' I will not accept ND-in-Docker to get JTA as a substitute for a correct Spring boundary. Reconciliation is a backstop, not the design. Modular monolith stays valid: refund-service can share the ledger transaction in-process.
commonMistakes: Catching the exception, logging it, and returning 200 so the API 'stays up.'
Calling this.refund() on the same class and thinking @Transactional ran.
Adding REQUIRES_NEW on the refund row so something always commits.
scoreRubric: Engineer: swallowed exception commits. Senior: proxy boundary, self-invocation, fail and retry. Staff: tests for rollbackFor and REQUIRES_NEW. Principal: money-defect standard; JTA/ND-in-Docker is not the fix; monolith in-process TX is valid.

topic: Spring Security vs Jakarta security on Liberty
question: BayPay's production payment-service is Spring Boot 3.5.5 on Java 21 with Spring Security in front of POST /api/v1/payments. Morgan Hale still has a Liberty lab with Jakarta Security annotations on an older WAR. A senior candidate: compare the two models, what you would keep equivalent for Harbor Bike Co, and what you would refuse to run as production.
followUps: Where does authentication live versus method authorization on each stack?
Why is mixing both filters on one Boot app a failure class?
expectedConcepts: Spring Security filter chain vs Jakarta Security / SecurityContext
Same product rules: mTLS or JWT at the edge, method security on money writes
Do not double-wrap or disable security 'for the lab' in prod
Liberty leftover is not the Fargate estate
engineerAnswer: Spring Security uses a filter chain and annotations like @PreAuthorize. Jakarta Security on Liberty uses HttpAuthenticationMechanism and @RolesAllowed. Both should deny an unauthenticated create.
seniorAnswer: I would keep one security stack per process. On Boot, the ALB or API Gateway plus Spring Security must authenticate the caller before Bean Validation; method security guards refund and admin. On Liberty, Jakarta Security plus server constraints do the same job. I will not enable both Spring Security and a leftover Jakarta filter on the same payment-service — that is an order-of-filters defect. I will not copy Liberty role names from dmgr-east into Fargate and call it done.
staffAnswer: I want a threat model: merchant identity, service-to-service, and actuator. Spring Security resource-server JWT is the Boot default I would review; Jakarta Security is fine on a true Liberty runtime with an owner. I reject security:none profiles in any image Jordan ships. I reject mixing BASIC in the WAR and OAuth on the ALB without a written identity story. I keep PAN out of tokens and logs.
principalAnswer: Production identity is the Boot path on Fargate, not Morgan Hale's cell. I will not fund ND-in-Docker so we can 'keep Jakarta Security.' I will not accept two authoritative security filters. Equivalent product rules — who may create, who may refund — must be written once and mapped, not reinvented per runtime. Modular monolith may host both payment and refund if the method security is consistent.
commonMistakes: Running Spring Security and Jakarta Security filters in one app 'to be safe.'
Disabling security in a prod-like profile because the lab used permitAll.
Treating the leftover Liberty cell as the production identity provider.
scoreRubric: Engineer: names both models and an unauthenticated deny. Senior: one stack per process, method security on writes. Staff: threat model, no security:none, no PAN. Principal: Boot is prod estate; no ND-in-Docker; consistent rules across modules.

topic: OpenEntityManagerInView in a payment worker
question: Someone enabled OpenEntityManagerInView on BayPay's Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.5.5 payment-service and the same default leaked into the transaction-worker that posts Harbor Bike Co ledger lines. Staff-level: what OSIV is for, why it is the wrong default on a payment worker, and what lazy-load failures you would rather see.
followUps: How does OSIV extend the persistence context past the @Transactional method?
What happens to connection hold time and Hikari under Avery Chen load?
expectedConcepts: OSIV keeps the EntityManager open for the view/request
Workers have no view; OSIV holds connections across extra work
LazyInitializationException is a signal to fix the query
Explicit transaction + fetch plan on the posting path
engineerAnswer: OpenEntityManagerInView keeps the JPA session open after the service method so a view can lazy-load. A worker is not a view, so I would turn it off and fetch what I need in the transaction.
seniorAnswer: On a web request OSIV can hide LazyInitializationException by holding the persistence context until the JSON is written — and it holds a JDBC connection while Jackson walks Payment. On transaction-worker there is no view; OSIV still opens an EM around the listener and can hold Hikari connections across JMS handling or extra logging. I disable spring.jpa.open-in-view for the worker (and I prefer it off for the API too). I want a fetch join or a DTO query inside @Transactional so Avery's post does not lazy-load Account after commit.
staffAnswer: I treat OSIV-on as a review fail for any money worker. I measure Hikari active time with OSIV on versus off under Harbor Bike Co replay. I would rather see a lazy-load exception in CI than a connection leak in prod. I set open-in-view=false in shared config and only allow a documented exception on a read-only admin UI, never on posting. I will not raise the pool to hide OSIV hold time, and I will not raise -Xmx.
principalAnswer: Default is OSIV off on payment-service and workers. Lazy load in a worker is a design bug, not a reason to keep the session open. I will not accept OSIV as 'Jakarta compatibility.' I will not move posting to ND-in-Docker to get a different persistence context. The modular monolith may share repositories; each process still owns its persistence-context lifetime.
commonMistakes: Leaving open-in-view true because it is the Boot default.
Raising Hikari max when OSIV holds connections through JSON or JMS.
Catching LazyInitializationException and opening a new session per field.
scoreRubric: Engineer: OSIV is for views; workers should fetch in-TX. Senior: connection hold and fetch plans. Staff: review fail, measure pool hold, OSIV off. Principal: org default off; no ND-in-Docker; per-process persistence lifetime.

topic: JTA vs Spring transactions when a JMS send must enlist
question: Staff interview: payment-service on Spring Boot 3.5.5 / Java 21 writes the Harbor Bike Co ledger and must send a JMS PaymentAuthorized event so notification-service fires. If the JDBC commit succeeds and the send fails, Avery Chen's merchant is wrong. When do you enlist JMS in JTA, when do you keep Spring DataSourceTransactionManager plus an outbox, and what do you refuse?
followUps: What does last-resource optimization risk on a Boot JVM without a full JTA manager?
How does the modular monolith change whether you need XA today?
expectedConcepts: Spring @Transactional is usually local JDBC, not XA
JTA/XA enlists JDBC and JMS in one 2PC
Transactional outbox avoids XA for most Boot deployments
Liberty JTA vs Boot Atomikos / Narayana — do not invent ND-in-Docker
engineerAnswer: A local Spring transaction commits the database even if the JMS send fails. JTA would enlist both. An outbox table written in the same JDBC transaction is another way.
seniorAnswer: Today the modular monolith can publish in-process and skip the broker. If we extract notification, I will not pretend @Transactional on the service enlists JMS. I prefer an outbox row in the same JDBC transaction, then a poller sends JMS — at-least-once with idempotent consumers. I would only take JTA/XA if we already have a manager we operate (Liberty JTA, or a reviewed Narayana) and we have tested rollback of both legs. I will not add Atomikos on a Friday SEV.
staffAnswer: I draw the failure: DB commit / send fail, send success / DB rollback, and broker replay. XA solves the first two at the cost of heuristic mixed outcomes and a transaction manager to page. Outbox solves them with operational simplicity and a reconciliation query Priya can alert on. I reject last-resource gamble as a silent default. I reject running this on ND-in-Docker 'because WAS had JTA.' If we are on Liberty for real, I will use the server's JTA with an owner, not a second TM.
principalAnswer: Default for Boot on Fargate is local Spring transactions plus outbox, not XA. JTA is allowed on a supported Liberty runtime with a named owner — not as a reason to keep a leftover cell, and never as ND-in-Docker. Dual-write without a pattern is a money defect. Modular monolith in-process notification remains a valid way to avoid this distributed problem entirely.
commonMistakes: Assuming @Transactional enlists JMS on a local DataSourceTransactionManager.
Adding XA mid-incident without a transaction manager owner.
Recommending ND-in-Docker to 'get JTA for free.'
scoreRubric: Engineer: local TX vs JTA vs outbox. Senior: prefers outbox, XA only if operated. Staff: failure matrix, rejects last-resource and ND-in-Docker. Principal: Boot+outbox default; Liberty JTA only with owner; in-process monolith valid.

topic: when Spring Boot on Liberty is the wrong runtime
question: A principal-level design review: Jordan Voss wants to run the Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.5.5 payment-service fat JAR inside WebSphere Liberty — or even ND — because 'that is our Java standard.' When is Spring Boot on Liberty the wrong runtime for BayPay, what would you run instead, and which answers fail this interview?
followUps: What operational contract does a Boot fat JAR on Fargate already satisfy?
When is Liberty actually the right host for a Jakarta-shaped module?
expectedConcepts: Boot on Fargate/K8s is the production payment-service shape
Liberty is right for Jakarta EE apps that use server JTA/JCA — not a decorative host
Never ND-in-Docker
Two classloaders / two metrics stacks are a cost, not a free standard
engineerAnswer: If the app is a Spring Boot fat JAR with its own Tomcat and Actuator, putting it inside Liberty adds a second server you do not need. I would run the JAR on Fargate.
seniorAnswer: Spring Boot on Liberty is wrong when we only want a process supervisor: we pay for two servlet stacks, two health models, and a classloader story we do not use. Harbor Bike Co creates already work on port 8080 with Boot actuators. Liberty is right when the module is Jakarta EE and needs server JTA, JCA, or a WAR the platform team already operates — with an owner, not a leftover cell. I will not wrap the Boot JAR in ND to satisfy a standard.
staffAnswer: I compare failure domains: Fargate task replace versus Liberty rolling app update versus a cell. I count who pages on classloader leaks versus OOM 137. If the only reason is 'Java apps go on Liberty,' I write a dissent. I allow a documented Liberty host for a Jakarta adapter, with Sam owning the image and Priya owning the SLO. I refuse mixing Boot actuators and Liberty monitor in one SEV without a map.
principalAnswer: I will sign Boot on Fargate for payment-service. I will sign Liberty for a genuine Jakarta workload with JTA/JCA and a platform owner. I will not sign Spring Boot on Liberty as a decorative standard, and I will never sign ND-in-Docker. Modular monolith on a single Boot JVM is valid. Leftover dmgr-east is not spare capacity and not a runtime strategy.
commonMistakes: Recommending ND-in-Docker as the enterprise-standard host.
Putting a Boot fat JAR on Liberty with no Jakarta features used.
Using Morgan Hale's leftover cell as production capacity.
scoreRubric: Engineer: fat JAR does not need a second server. Senior: when Liberty is real vs decorative. Staff: failure-domain comparison and dissent. Principal: Boot/Fargate for payments; Liberty only for Jakarta-with-owner; never ND-in-Docker.

topic: Actuator exposure vs production attack surface
question: Jordan Voss enabled Spring Boot 3.5.5 Actuator on payment-service so Priya Nair can scrape health. A developer opened /actuator/env and /actuator/heapdump on the ALB hostname. In this Java 21 interview, what do you expose, what do you lock down, and how do liveness and readiness stay available for Harbor Bike Co traffic without handing out the process?
followUps: Which two health endpoints does the Fargate target group need?
Why is heapdump on a public path a SEV-class exposure?
expectedConcepts: Expose liveness and readiness only on the probe path
env, heapdump, logfile, beans are sensitive
Separate management port / network policy
No PAN or secrets in actuator output
engineerAnswer: I would expose /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness for probes. I would not expose env or heapdump on the public ALB.
seniorAnswer: Probes stay on 8080 or a management port that only the load balancer and kubelet can reach. I set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include to health — maybe prometheus on a scrape network — and I leave heapdump, env, configprops, threaddump off the internet. A heapdump endpoint is a production freeze and a PII path. Env can leak datasource URLs. Harbor Bike Co creates do not need those endpoints to succeed.
staffAnswer: I want a written exposure list, a network policy, and a test that the ALB hostname returns 404 or 401 for /actuator/env. I review that health groups do not include downstream payment rails in liveness — fail readiness, not liveness, when Hikari is exhausted. I reject Actuator plus Spring Security permitAll. I reject attaching a heapdump from Actuator to Slack. No PAN, no BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in env.
principalAnswer: Actuator is part of the production attack surface, not a convenience switch. I will sign health and authenticated metrics; I will not sign anonymous dump endpoints. I will not accept 'we needed it for the SEV' as a reason to leave heapdump on. I will not put Actuator on ND-in-Docker to copy WAS admin. Modular monolith means one careful exposure list, not five open admin UIs.
commonMistakes: Exposing * or heapdump/env on the public hostname.
Putting secrets or PAN into environment variables that /actuator/env would show.
Failing liveness when a dependency is down and looping restarts.
scoreRubric: Engineer: health only, no public dumps. Senior: include-list, management port, readiness vs liveness. Staff: network policy, tests, no secrets. Principal: attack surface standard; no dump-for-SEV; no ND-in-Docker admin.

topic: Testcontainers strategy for payment persistence
question: Riley Okonkwo's payment-service tests on Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.5.5 use H2 for most slices and a Testcontainers Postgres for Harbor Bike Co create and replay. Design the strategy: what runs in H2, what must run in Postgres, and how you keep CI honest without making every test start a database.
followUps: Which idempotency or locking behaviors will H2 lie about?
How do you share one container across a test class without leaking rows between Avery cases?
expectedConcepts: H2 for unit/slice; Testcontainers for SQL fidelity
Unique constraints, isolation, JSON/UUID types
Reuse containers; truncate or transactional rollback between tests
No PAN in fixtures; DemoIds only
engineerAnswer: I use H2 for fast unit tests and Testcontainers Postgres for API tests that depend on real constraints, like idempotency unique keys for Avery's create.
seniorAnswer: H2 will not faithfully do Postgres unique violations, isolation, or some types. PaymentApiIT and replay tests should use Testcontainers. Domain tests for Money and the state machine stay in-memory. I reuse one Postgres container per class, wrap each test in a transaction or truncate tables, and I never put PAN in fixtures — DemoIds and amounts only. I fail the build if the container cannot start rather than silently falling back to H2 for those ITs.
staffAnswer: I split the suite so PR CI runs unit plus one Postgres IT module, and nightly runs the heavier concurrency create test. I pin the Postgres image version Jordan also uses in paper prod notes. I watch for tests that @DirtiesContext the whole Spring Boot 3.5.5 app per method. I reject a strategy that needs Docker-in-ND or a shared dev cell database. Flyway/Liquibase must run against the same container the IT uses.
principalAnswer: Persistence tests that guard money invariants run on real Postgres. That is a quality gate, not optional local flavor. I will not accept H2-only as the merge bar for idempotency. I will not accept ND-in-Docker as the Testcontainers host. The modular monolith can share one test database schema across modules; we do not need a database per extracted service to test uniqueness.
commonMistakes: Running idempotency uniqueness only on H2 and calling it done.
Starting a new container per test method and blowing CI time.
Loading PAN or live passwords into test fixtures.
scoreRubric: Engineer: H2 vs Testcontainers split. Senior: constraint fidelity, reuse, no PAN. Staff: CI layers, pinned image, migrations. Principal: Postgres as merge bar for money tests; no ND-in-Docker; shared schema valid.

topic: Jakarta EE mapping for a Spring-trained team
question: Staff coaching: BayPay's payment-service team is Spring Boot 3.5.5 / Java 21 fluent and must read a Jakarta EE Liberty module Morgan Hale left behind. Map Spring ideas to Jakarta for them — injection, transactions, validation, persistence — and tell me what you would not tell them to rewrite first.
followUps: What is the Jakarta pair for @Service plus constructor injection?
Where does @Transactional map, and where does UserTransaction appear?
expectedConcepts: @Service/@Component → @ApplicationScoped or @Stateless
Constructor @Autowired → @Inject
Spring @Transactional → Jakarta @Transactional / JTA
Bean Validation and JPA names already shared; do not rewrite the domain first
engineerAnswer: Spring @Service with a constructor becomes a CDI bean with @Inject. @Transactional has a Jakarta name too. @Valid and JPA look familiar. I would not start by rewriting Money.
seniorAnswer: I map PaymentApplicationService to an @ApplicationScoped or @Stateless bean with constructor @Inject of repositories. Spring's @Transactional maps to Jakarta transaction interceptor or container JTA — same 'exceptions must leave the boundary' rule. CreatePaymentRequest validation is already Jakarta Bean Validation. JPA entities in shared stay. I teach the team the server's DataSource and JTA, not a new domain model. I do not tell them to extract microservices to avoid learning CDI.
staffAnswer: I run a pairing map: IoC, TX, validation, persistence, security, messaging. I call out the traps: Spring proxies versus CDI interceptors, self-invocation still skips TX, OSIV is not a Jakarta default, and Liberty classloaders are a different leak class. I keep production payment-service on Boot; the Liberty module is a port, not a surprise rewrite. I schedule time for JNDI and JTA labs, not for ND-in-Docker. I use Avery Chen create as the same acceptance test on both stacks.
principalAnswer: I will fund a mapping guide and a shared domain, not a rewrite of Harbor Bike Co into two languages of money. Spring-trained engineers should become bilingual; they should not be told the modular monolith is invalid or that ND-in-Docker is how you learn Jakarta. Boot remains the production runtime unless a Jakarta-only adapter is evidenced. Same status codes, same idempotency, same no-PAN rule.
commonMistakes: Telling the team to rewrite the domain before they can map injection and TX.
Equating Spring @Transactional with a local TX while the Liberty module is JTA without saying so.
Recommending ND-in-Docker as the Jakarta training environment.
scoreRubric: Engineer: basic annotation map, do not rewrite Money. Senior: CDI vs Spring, TX boundary, shared JPA. Staff: trap list, pairing plan, same acceptance test. Principal: bilingual team, monolith valid, Boot stays prod, never ND-in-Docker.

topic: cell, DMGR, node agent and application server
question: BayPay Financial Services still runs its source estate on traditional WebSphere ND cell BayPayCell. Explain the cell, dmgr-east, a node agent such as nodeagent-pay-2, and an application server such as Pay1. What still serves Harbor Bike Co if dmgr-east is down? This is not a greenfield design.
followUps: What can Morgan Hale no longer do if nodeagent-pay-2 is down while Pay2 and Pay3 stay STARTED?
Why is ihs-east not a federated WAS node, and why would you refuse a second cell for a new FX quote service?
expectedConcepts: BayPayCell is a management domain, not a serving JVM
dmgr-east owns the master repository and console; it does not run payment.ear
node agent syncs and starts/stops servers; application servers serve /payment
Traditional ND is source estate to operate and leave
engineerAnswer: The cell is the admin unit. dmgr-east on was-dmgr-east.baypay.example hosts the console and master config. node-pay-1 and node-pay-2 are federated machines with nodeagent-pay-1 and nodeagent-pay-2. Pay1, Pay2, and Pay3 are the JVMs that run payment.ear. Merchants hit those members through ihs-east, never the DMGR. If dmgr-east is down, already-started Pay members keep serving Avery Chen.
seniorAnswer: I separate management from traffic. Killing dmgr-east does not stop POST /payment if PaymentCluster is already up. A down nodeagent-pay-2 means Morgan cannot reliably sync, start, or stop Pay2 and Pay3 from the cell, but those JVMs can keep running. I would not bounce dmgr-east to fix a merchant 500 on Pay2. I read node-agent health and member state first. ihs-east is IBM HTTP Server plus the plugin, not a federated node. This topology is what we inherited, not what I would draw for a new service.
staffAnswer: On a page I name the process that can actually change Avery Chen's outcome. Riley owns Pay1–Pay3. Morgan owns cell documents and sync. Priya cares whether plugin rotation still lists healthy members. A DMGR outage is an admin outage; a Pay2 hang is a payment outage. I will not treat a down node agent as 'the cell is dead' while Pay1 is still posting. I also will not propose stuffing this cell into Docker. I operate BayPayCell until cutover and I keep the exit (Liberty or Boot) on the table instead of growing another Deployment Manager.
principalAnswer: BayPayCell is a shrinking source estate. I will fund runbooks and diagnostics so we do not bounce the wrong JVM, and I will not fund a second ND cell for greenfield work. The architectural control is: serving processes are disposable members; the DMGR is a config authority we intend to retire. If someone asks for a new payment product on a new cell, I send them to Spring Boot 3.5.5 or Liberty server.xml. I will not accept 'rebuild BayPayCell in Kubernetes' as modernization. Paper topology is enough; no live cell is required to answer this.
commonMistakes: Bouncing dmgr-east to fix a merchant failure on Pay2
Treating a down node agent as proof that application servers have stopped
Recommending a new traditional ND cell as the greenfield payment platform
scoreRubric: Engineer: names cell, DMGR, node agent, and serving JVM with locked BayPayCell names and says merchants do not hit dmgr-east. Senior: predicts dmgr-down versus node-agent-down behavior and refuses a DMGR bounce as stabilize. Staff: assigns Riley/Morgan/Priya ownership and treats ND as operated source estate, not a Docker project. Principal: refuses a second cell for greenfield and frames Liberty/Boot as the exit.

topic: plugin-cfg and web server routing to a cluster
question: Harbor Bike Co reaches payment.ear through ihs-east.baypay.example. How does plugin-cfg.xml decide which PaymentCluster member receives /payment, and what goes wrong if Jordan Voss adds Pay3 but nobody propagates the plugin?
followUps: How do you drain Pay2 before a rolling EAR update using the plugin rather than hoping TCP health is enough?
What is the difference between cluster membership Morgan sees and the rotation file Priya reads on ihs-east?
expectedConcepts: plugin-cfg.xml lists clusters, member host/port, and URI groups
Regenerate and propagate is a separate step from adding a cluster member
Stale plugin sends traffic to drained JVMs or never hits new members
Drain via plugin before stopping a member
engineerAnswer: ihs-east reads plugin-cfg.xml. That file lists PaymentCluster transports and URI groups such as /payment/*. The plugin is not the cell. After Morgan adds Pay3, someone must regenerate the plugin and copy it to ihs-east. If that step is skipped, Pay3 is in the cluster and never receives merchant traffic.
seniorAnswer: I treat plugin-cfg.xml as the merchant rotation file. Cluster membership in the console can disagree with what ihs-east actually routes. A quiet miss is install success plus no propagate: capacity planning that counted three members is fiction. Before I stop Pay2 I remove it from the plugin or mark it down, wait for in-flight work, then bounce that JVM. I put it back only after a synthetic /payment check I trust, not after TCP accept alone.
staffAnswer: On an intermittent 50/50 merchant failure I compare plugin membership to STARTED members and to node sync, not just 'the cluster is up.' Wrong ports, a missing Pay3, or a leftover host after a drain are first-class evidence. I will not ripple-stop PaymentCluster to 'refresh the plugin.' I regenerate, propagate, and prove ihs-east has the new file. This is source-estate operations. I do not invent a live generate on a laptop cell to answer the question.
principalAnswer: Routing truth for traditional WAS sits at the edge file, not in the admin console screenshot. I want a release contract: membership change, plugin regenerate, propagate, prove, then serve. That contract is why we are leaving for an ALB or Ingress that is declared in git — but until cutover, plugin drift is a payment incident class. I will not dual-home merchants to the leftover IHS path as 'HA' once Boot is the front door.
commonMistakes: Assuming a STARTED cluster member is in rotation because the console shows three members
Restarting Pay1 to fix a stale plugin-cfg.xml on ihs-east
Treating TCP accept on the member port as proof the plugin should keep sending POSTs
scoreRubric: Engineer: describes plugin-cfg.xml as the IHS rotation file and names regenerate/propagate. Senior: drains via plugin before stop and distrusts TCP-only health. Staff: diagnoses console-versus-plugin drift without a cluster bounce. Principal: makes edge-file truth a release contract and refuses leftover IHS as HA after cutover.

topic: JNDI DataSource vs Spring datasource on ND
question: payment.ear on PaymentCluster looks up jdbc/baypay from cell JNDI. The teaching runtime payment-service on Spring Boot 3.5.5 uses Hikari through BAYPAY_DB_* . Compare those two datasource models. What breaks if someone tries to run the Boot app as another ear that still expects the cell-scoped name?
followUps: Why is a shared cell-scoped jdbc/baypay a modernization smell for payment versus refund?
Where would Liberty bind jdbc/baypay-payment instead, and why not reuse the historic name?
expectedConcepts: WAS JNDI DataSource is cell-owned; Spring datasource is process-owned
jdbc/baypay shared across ears is a smell
Liberty/Boot isolate jdbc/baypay-payment and BAYPAY_DB_*
NameNotFoundException versus silent wrong-pool success
engineerAnswer: On ND, Morgan defines jdbc/baypay in the cell and payment.ear looks it up. The pool lives in the WAS JDBC provider, historically maxConnections 50 on PaymentCluster. Boot does not ask the cell. It builds Hikari from environment variables. If I deploy the Boot JAR as if it were payment.ear and leave a lookup for jdbc/baypay, I either get NameNotFoundException or I attach to the leftover shared pool.
seniorAnswer: The operational difference is ownership. On the cell, a pool change is a cell document plus sync. On Boot, a pool change is application config and a new revision. I will not point Spring at the cell JNDI 'to reuse connections.' That couples a disposable process to BayPayCell. Shared jdbc/baypay also means a refund report can starve authorize. Isolated names jdbc/baypay-payment and jdbc/baypay-refund exist so those teams cannot share a max. jdbc/baypayXA is not even on every node today — cloning that hole is not compatibility.
staffAnswer: I treat the two models as different estates. INCIDENT-shaped pool pain on ND is PMI on jdbc/baypay. On Boot it is Hikari USE on the task. Dual-writing those graphs is a method fail. A 'temporary' JNDI lookup from Boot to the cell is how leftover Morgan Hale operations become a production dependency again. I will fail a design review that keeps one cell-wide pool 'until Liberty features are done.' Isolation is the first cut, not a later cleanup. No live cell is required to say that; TOPOLOGY.md already names the smell.
principalAnswer: Datasource scope is an architecture control. Cell JNDI made thin ears possible and made blast radius cell-wide. The exit is process-owned pools with secrets outside the repo, whether Liberty server.xml or Spring Boot. I will not accept a hybrid where new Java 21 services look up WebSphere:cell/... names. That is not a migration; it is a new coupling. Greenfield BayPay work does not get a DataSource in BayPayCell.
commonMistakes: Reusing jdbc/baypay from Boot or Liberty so 'the name stays familiar'
Assuming Spring can bind to WAS cell JNDI without taking a hard dependency on the leftover estate
Treating jdbc/baypayXA as a required Liberty feature because it existed on some nodes
scoreRubric: Engineer: contrasts cell JNDI lookup with Spring/Hikari env config. Senior: isolates payment vs refund pools and rejects Boot-on-cell JNDI. Staff: refuses dual-writing ND PMI and Boot Hikari as one graph. Principal: treats datasource scope as an estate decision and forbids new cell bindings.

topic: session affinity vs stateless payment APIs
question: Morgan Hale offers to enable session affinity on ihs-east so Harbor Bike Co 'stays on Pay2' during a PaymentCluster rollout. Should the BayPay payment API be sticky? How does that interact with a stateless POST /payment and Idempotency-Key?
followUps: Where might leftover HttpSession or LTPA still appear on the cell, and why is that not a reason to pin payment POSTs?
What fails for Avery Chen if Pay2 dies and affinity still points at it?
expectedConcepts: Payment API is sessionless; sticky sessions are a smell
Idempotency-Key must work on any healthy member
Affinity turns a member death into a pinned outage
LTPA/IHS SSL are not reasons to store payment state in the JVM
engineerAnswer: The payment API should stay sessionless. A create is a POST with an Idempotency-Key, not a shopping-cart HttpSession. If ihs-east pins Harbor Bike Co to Pay2, a hung Pay2 becomes that merchant's only path. Any healthy Pay member should be able to see the same idempotency record and return the same paymentId.
seniorAnswer: I refuse sticky sessions for /payment. Affinity is a workaround for server-side session state we should not have. During a rolling EAR update I drain via plugin, I do not enable affinity 'so the browser finishes.' If we still have LTPA for some leftover UI on the cell, that is a different URI group. I will not let that policy cover the payment API. Stateless members plus a shared store for idempotency is how we survive Pay2 dying mid-rollout.
staffAnswer: I ask what state the affinity is protecting. If the answer is 'in-memory authorize progress,' that is a defect, not a plugin setting. I want evidence: session cookies on /payment, or none. PMI session counts on Pay2 after a drain are a smell. Staff-level stabilize is remove affinity if it was added as a hotfix, fail the bad member out of the plugin, and keep idempotency on a store every member can read. I will not recommend sticky sessions as the path to Liberty or Boot either — those runtimes should stay sessionless too.
principalAnswer: Session affinity on a payment API is an architecture smell I will not standardize. It couples merchant success to one JVM and fights every rolling deploy. The platform contract is: any replica may accept the POST; exactly-once business effect is the idempotency store, not the plugin cookie. I will allow affinity only for a named leftover UI with an exit date, never for authorize. This answer does not require a live cell; it is a design refusal.
commonMistakes: Enabling IHS sticky sessions so a rollout 'does not break in-flight browsers'
Storing authorize progress in HttpSession on Pay2
Assuming LTPA cookies mean the payment API must be sticky
scoreRubric: Engineer: states the payment API is sessionless and affinity pins outages. Senior: drains without sticky sessions and keeps idempotency member-independent. Staff: treats affinity as a defect signal and refuses it on the Liberty/Boot exit. Principal: makes sessionless replicas a platform contract with a dated exception only for leftover UI.

topic: classloader policy parent-first vs parent-last
question: payment.ear on BayPayCell is set to PARENT_LAST / application-first because an older SLF4J and a JDBC driver in the EAR disagree with the server. Explain parent-first versus parent-last, and what that policy means when we move toward Liberty or Spring Boot.
followUps: What happens if Pay1 is parent-first and Pay2 is parent-last after a partial sync?
Why is a WAS shared library not a Liberty feature you enable to 'keep compatibility'?
expectedConcepts: Parent-first prefers server classes; parent-last prefers the application
PARENT_LAST hides version conflicts instead of fixing the classpath
Liberty/Boot need an honest dependency set, not a loader trick
Partial sync can make members disagree on which class wins
engineerAnswer: Parent-first means the WAS server classloader wins; the ear sees IBM and server copies first. Parent-last / application-first means the ear's JARs win, which is how teams hide a different slf4j or driver from the parent. That flag is cell policy. Liberty's default is simpler and app-owned. Boot is a fat JAR with one classpath. The trick does not travel.
seniorAnswer: I treat PARENT_LAST as a finding, not a portable setting. If payment.ear only starts because it hid a driver, the assessment is 'fix the classpath,' not 'set the same flag on Liberty.' A worse production case is mixed policy after a bad sync: Pay1 and Pay2 resolve different classes for the same Idempotency-Key path. I would rather pin one driver in the ear and go parent-first, or isolate the library properly, than keep application-first as folklore.
staffAnswer: Classloader policy is how WAS made shared server libraries survivable. It is also how we get NoClassDefFoundError that only happens on Pay3. In a compatibility review I score PARENT_LAST and server-scoped shared libraries as cannot-lift-and-shift. I will not accept 'enable a classloading feature' as the Liberty plan. I want a dependency inventory and a single winner for JDBC and logging. No live cell is required; the ear's ibm binding and loader setting on paper is enough.
principalAnswer: Loader tricks are technical debt with an operational tax. I will not carry WAS PARENT_LAST into the target estate as a control. The architecture rule is: one process, one declared classpath, features or Spring starters named in git. If an ear cannot start without hiding server classes, it is a rewrite candidate, not a wave-2 canary. I fund the classpath cleanup in wave 0 so we do not discover it on Avery Chen.
commonMistakes: Copying PARENT_LAST onto Liberty as the compatibility plan
Leaving mixed loader policies across PaymentCluster members after a partial deploy
Using a server-scoped shared library to 'solve' a Boot or Liberty conflict
scoreRubric: Engineer: defines parent-first vs parent-last and says the trick does not travel. Senior: treats PARENT_LAST as a classpath finding and flags mixed-member policy. Staff: scores loader tricks as cannot-lift-and-shift in the assessment. Principal: refuses loader policy as a target-estate control and funds wave-0 cleanup.

topic: why one cluster member stops consuming JMS
question: Priya Nair pages that Pay2 is STARTED but has stopped consuming jms/paymentEvents on SIBus BayPayBus, while Pay1 and Pay3 still drain the queue. How do you investigate one cluster member that stopped consuming JMS? Give a method, not a lucky root cause.
followUps: What evidence would tell you the listener is hung versus the member never joined the bus destination?
Why is recycling PaymentCluster the wrong first move?
expectedConcepts: Per-member JMS listener state versus bus destination state
Hung consumer, paused MDB, or connection-factory failure as symptom classes
Preserve stacks; do not ripple-stop the cluster
SIBus does not lift-and-shift; this is source-estate ops
engineerAnswer: I would look at Pay2 only first: MDB or listener status, JMS connection factory, and whether that JVM still has a consumer on jms/paymentEvents. I would compare PMI or FFDC on Pay2 to Pay1. A STARTED JVM can still have a dead listener. I would not restart the whole PaymentCluster and I would not touch dmgr-east.
seniorAnswer: Method: prove the symptom is member-local. If the bus still has depth and Pay1/Pay3 consume, the destination is not 'down.' Classes I rank unproven: hung listener thread, exhausted JMS session pool on Pay2, destination not activated after a sync, or a stuck transaction holding the consumer. First stabilize is keep Pay1/Pay3 serving and consuming; drain Pay2 from the plugin if HTTP is also sick. I take a thread dump on Pay2 before anyone recycles it. A bounce without stacks loses the only evidence.
staffAnswer: Staff work is to keep HTTP authorize and async consume as separate questions. A member can serve /payment and still starve events, or the reverse. I ask Morgan for bus membership and activation on Pay2, Riley for listener/MDB config that last synced, and Priya for queue depth plus per-member consume rates. I will not declare a root cause from the title 'stopped consuming.' I will not enable a JMS feature on Liberty as the hotfix. If we stabilize by leaving Pay2 out of the plugin and out of the consumer set, that is an explicit degrade, not a silent hope.
principalAnswer: This incident class is why BayPayBus is on the cannot-lift-and-shift list. I will pay for source-estate diagnostics, and I will not grow more MDBs on the cell. The strategic question after stabilize is whether eventing should already be off SIBus for the Boot path. I will not accept 'restart the cluster' as culture, and I will not accept a new ear on PaymentCluster as the fix. The spoken answer is a method; a live bus is not required.
commonMistakes: Ripple-stopping PaymentCluster or bouncing dmgr-east as the first action
Declaring a single root cause from the queue name without per-member evidence
Treating 'STARTED' as proof the JMS listener is consuming
scoreRubric: Engineer: compares Pay2 listener state to other members and avoids a cluster bounce. Senior: ranks unproven symptom classes and dumps threads before recycle. Staff: splits HTTP vs consume, assigns owners, and states an explicit degrade. Principal: ties the class to leaving SIBus and refuses new MDBs on the cell.

topic: JDBC pool exhaustion vs database saturation
question: Harbor Bike Co sees slow POST /payment. Morgan Hale says jdbc/baypay is at maxConnections 50. Sam's DBA chat says db-east.baypay.example is 'busy.' How do you tell WAS JDBC pool exhaustion from database saturation, and what do you refuse to do first?
followUps: What PMI or thread-dump signals point at waiters in the pool versus waiters inside PostgreSQL?
Why is raising maxConnections without looking at in-flight work a dangerous 'fix'?
expectedConcepts: Pool waiters vs database CPU/locks/connections
Hung threads holding checkouts
Shared jdbc/baypay can couple refund reporting to authorize
Do not bounce the cell or set -Xmx to a cgroup as capacity
engineerAnswer: Pool exhaustion means threads are waiting for a connection from jdbc/baypay while active equals max. Database saturation means connections that did check out are slow or blocked in SQL. I look at pool waiting versus active, and at whether db-east sessions are running or idle-in-transaction. I do not recycle PaymentCluster as the first step.
seniorAnswer: I split the graphs. If PMI shows waiters and active=50, the next question is who holds the 50. A thread dump with many threads parked on getConnection is pool wait. Stacks in the driver on a query, plus db-east wait events, is database saturation that happens to fill the pool. Raising maxConnections can make a saturated database worse. I stabilize by shedding work or failing a sick member out of the plugin, not by opening more sessions. I also check whether refund reporting is on the same jdbc/baypay — that shared pool is a known smell.
staffAnswer: Staff diagnosis is two clocks: application checkout wait and database execution. I will not accept 'the database is down' or 'the pool is the RCA' without both. I keep hypotheses unproven. I will not dual-write leftover cell PMI onto a Boot Hikari incident later. Remediation that needs approval: isolate reporting, lower inbound via plugin, fix the holder leak if dumps show it. I refuse ND-in-Docker, a leftover cell bounce as capacity, and any suggestion that heap should equal a container limit — that is the wrong estate and the wrong knob.
principalAnswer: This class is why I will not keep one cell-scoped pool. Isolation and backpressure are cheaper than another 50 connections. I want a written rule: pool max is sized from in-flight work, not from fear, and it is never a substitute for database capacity. After the incident I fund the Liberty/Boot isolated DataSources, not a larger shared jdbc/baypay. Lucky 'it's the database' without method does not pass staff.
commonMistakes: Raising maxConnections immediately or bouncing PaymentCluster to 'free the pool'
Treating pool waiters as proof the database is down, or the reverse, without both signals
Using a leftover dmgr-east bounce or -Xmx equal to a memory limit as a capacity move
scoreRubric: Engineer: defines pool wait vs SQL wait and avoids a cluster recycle. Senior: uses PMI plus stacks and refuses a blind maxConnections raise. Staff: keeps dual hypotheses, names shared-pool smell, and refuses wrong-estate knobs. Principal: converts the incident into isolated pools and a sizing rule.

topic: rollout that failed after EAR update
question: Jordan Voss updated payment.ear on PaymentCluster. The console shows STARTED on members, but Harbor Bike Co now sees intermittent failures for the same Idempotency-Key. How do you work a rollout that failed after an EAR update? Use symptom classes, not a memorized instructor RCA.
followUps: What is the difference between a completed node sync and a member that merely reports STARTED?
How would you roll back one member without ripple-stopping the cluster?
expectedConcepts: STARTED is not same-version
Sync, plugin membership, and class/binding mismatch as classes
Drain, compare bits, roll back a member
Do not bounce dmgr-east
engineerAnswer: I would not trust STARTED. I would ask which edition each of Pay1, Pay2, and Pay3 actually has, and whether node sync finished on node-pay-2. Intermittent same-key failures sound like members disagree. I would drain a suspect member at ihs-east and compare logs, not restart dmgr-east.
seniorAnswer: Classes I rank: incomplete sync, plugin still routing to a drained or old transport, failed partial activate, or mixed class/bindings across members. Stabilize is stop sending new POSTs to the bad member via plugin-cfg, keep the last known good member in rotation, and do not ripple-stop. Rollback is re-target the previous ear on that member after a sync you can prove, then put it back in the plugin. I will not call this 'fine' because the application state is STARTED.
staffAnswer: Staff method is a version matrix: ear file name, node repository generation, plugin file timestamp on ihs-east, and one successful synthetic /payment on each member. I assign Jordan the change window, Morgan the sync, Priya the plugin, Riley the member logs. Lucky 'it was the plugin' or 'it was sync' without those four columns does not close the incident. I communicate intermittent as mixed estate, not as random network. I refuse a new ear on PaymentCluster as the greenfield path; this is how we leave, not how we grow.
principalAnswer: A payment platform cannot have 'probably the same bits.' I want immutable artifacts and an edge that is declared, which is why Boot on ECS or Kubernetes is the target. Until then the rollout contract on the cell is: one edition, proven sync, proven plugin, member-by-member drain. I will not accept console STARTED as the release gate. I also will not let this incident become a reason to keep investing in ND instead of finishing wave 2.
commonMistakes: Treating STARTED as proof every member runs the new ear
Ripple-stopping PaymentCluster or bouncing dmgr-east after a bad deploy
Naming a single instructor-lab root cause instead of working version/sync/plugin classes
scoreRubric: Engineer: distrusts STARTED and compares members. Senior: drains via plugin and rolls back one member with a proven sync. Staff: uses a version matrix across roles and refuses a lucky RCA word. Principal: turns the miss into an immutable-artifact contract and keeps the exit funded.

topic: Liberty feature set as an architecture control
question: Jordan Voss wants to enable 'whatever Liberty features payment.ear might need' on the wave-2 canary so the assessment goes faster. Why is the Liberty feature set an architecture control for BayPay, not a compatibility checklist?
followUps: Which four teaching features does BayPay write first, and what does adding a JMS or WS feature imply?
How do features compare to Spring Boot starters as a surface-area decision?
expectedConcepts: featureManager is an explicit runtime surface
servlet-6.0 jdbc-4.3 jndi-1.0 persistence-3.1 as the teaching set
Enabling JMS/WS recreates cell coupling
Smaller feature set is a security and ops control
engineerAnswer: Liberty starts with the features you list in server.xml. BayPay's teaching set is servlet-6.0, jdbc-4.3, jndi-1.0, and persistence-3.1. If I enable extra features 'just in case,' I grow the runtime I have to patch and understand. A JMS feature does not recreate BayPayBus.
seniorAnswer: I treat each feature as a dependency we now own. jdbc-4.3 plus isolated jdbc/baypay-payment is enough for the war path. Adding messaging or WS features because the old ear had admin-console bindings is how we drag SIBus and WS-* into the target. I would rather fail the assessment honestly and keep the ear on ND than enable a kitchen-sink featureManager on the canary.
staffAnswer: Staff review looks at featureManager the way we look at Spring starters: every enabled API is attack surface, thread pools, and an ops manual. I want a written allow-list. A PR that adds a feature to 'make the ear start' needs the same bar as a new production dependency. I also want refund and payment Liberty processes to declare their own features, not inherit a cell-shaped supermodule. Paper server.xml is enough; I do not need a live Liberty JVM to reject kitchen-sink features.
principalAnswer: Features are how Liberty encodes architecture. I use them to forbid a second cell: the target is a small, named runtime, not 'WAS without the DMGR.' I will not sign a wave-2 canary whose featureManager is an inventory of every IBM API payment.ear ever touched. If the business still needs SIBus semantics, that is a broker decision or a stay-on-ND decision, not a feature checkbox. The same control applies to Boot: I will not add starters that recreate cell services either.
commonMistakes: Enabling every possible Liberty feature so the ear starts
Believing a JMS feature is a lift-and-shift of SIBus BayPayBus
Sharing one kitchen-sink server.xml across payment and refund
scoreRubric: Engineer: names the teaching feature set and says extras have cost. Senior: refuses kitchen-sink features as a fake assessment pass. Staff: treat features as an allow-listed production dependency. Principal: uses featureManager as the anti-cell control and keeps SIBus off the canary.

topic: migration waves and rollback for a bank platform
question: Design migration waves and rollback for BayPay leaving BayPayCell. The locked teaching waves are inventory, refund on Liberty, payment canary, then decommission ND after an SLO hold. How do you roll back a bank platform without a second DMGR?
followUps: Why is refund wave 1 even when refund.ear may be 'harder' on SIBus?
What does dual-run mean for jdbc/baypay versus isolated Liberty pools?
expectedConcepts: Waves 0–3: inventory, refund, payment canary, decommission
Rollback is edge plus artifact, not a new cell
Dual-run and SLO hold before killing ND
Wave 0 has no runtime rollback because nothing moved
engineerAnswer: Wave 0 is inventory only. Wave 1 moves refund to Liberty first because volume is lower, not because refund is simple. Wave 2 canaries payment. Wave 3 decommissions ND after we hold the SLO. Rollback is send traffic back to the previous estate or previous revision, not stand up dmgr-west.
seniorAnswer: Each wave has an edge switch and a proven last-good. For Liberty that is ihs-east URI groups or a later ALB rule. For Boot it is a previous ECS revision or Deployment. Dual-run means both estates can complete a refund or a payment without sharing jdbc/baypay. Isolated pools, separate logs, same Idempotency-Key store or a carefully mapped one. I will not roll back by federating a new node. I will not mark wave 3 done because the console is quiet.
staffAnswer: Staff rollback is a written matrix: who flips the edge, how long dual-run lasts, what SLO we hold, and what we do with in-flight SIBus messages that the Liberty war does not consume. Wave 0 has no runtime rollback — if the assessment is wrong we have not moved traffic. That is why honesty in the assessment is the control. I keep BayPayCell read-only for new features during wave 2. Jordan does not ship new ears 'while we canary.' Comms name the estate merchants are on. I will not fail over to the leftover cell after Boot is the front door.
principalAnswer: A bank platform rollback is a product contract: time to reverse the edge, data compatibility, and a freeze on the estate we are leaving. I sequence refund first to learn Liberty ops at lower authorize risk, even if refund messaging is ugly — ugly stays or gets a broker, it does not become a silent feature. I will not buy a second traditional cell as a bunker, and I will not call Kubernetes-shaped ND a wave. Decommission is a dated decision after the SLO hold, not an infinite dual-run that becomes the new production.
commonMistakes: Standing up a second DMGR or 'ND in Kubernetes' as the rollback bunker
Moving payment first because it is the 'real' app, or skipping wave-0 inventory
Sharing jdbc/baypay during dual-run and calling that isolation
scoreRubric: Engineer: recites waves 0–3 and rollback-to-previous-estate. Senior: names edge switch, dual-run isolation, and last-good artifacts. Staff: writes in-flight messaging and freeze rules; no leftover-cell failover after Boot. Principal: treats rollback as a product contract and dates decommission after an SLO hold.

topic: server.xml vs traditional admin console
question: Contrast Liberty server.xml on disk with the traditional BayPayCell admin console. Who can change jdbc/baypay-payment in each world, and how would Riley Okonkwo see that change in an incident?
followUps: Where do server.env and variables fit so secrets are not committed in XML?
Why is 'we can still click the Liberty admin center like the DMGR' a smell?
expectedConcepts: server.xml is process-owned, reviewable config
Admin console is cell documents plus sync
server.env / variables for BAYPAY_DB_*
Git history versus console folklore
engineerAnswer: On ND, Morgan changes a DataSource in the admin console and syncs the node. The file of record is the cell repository. On Liberty, jdbc/baypay-payment lives in server.xml next to featureManager and the war. Riley can open the XML and server.env in the change ticket. He does not need the DMGR to see what should be running.
seniorAnswer: The console is a UI over a master repository. That is powerful and opaque. Two Pay members can disagree until sync finishes. server.xml is the desired state of one process. I review it like application-prod.yml. Secrets stay in server.env or the platform secret store, not in committed XML. If someone uses a Liberty admin center as a second DMGR, we have reproduced the folklore problem. I want the file in git.
staffAnswer: Staff incident method changes with the config model. On the cell I ask for sync generation and console history. On Liberty I ask for the git SHA and the rendered server.env on that host or container. I will not accept 'Morgan clicked it' as a change record for a payment canary. I also will not run a live console to answer an interview; paper XML is the artifact.
principalAnswer: Config-as-files is why Liberty is an exit and ND is not. I will not invest in making the admin console prettier. The control is: every production process can be explained from a reviewed file plus an external secret. Teams that recreate a cell by putting twenty Liberty servers behind an unofficial console have failed the migration. Boot remains the teaching greenfield; Liberty is the ear-compatible file-based path.
commonMistakes: Treating the Liberty admin center as a replacement Deployment Manager
Committing BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in server.xml
Assuming a console click is already live on every PaymentCluster member
scoreRubric: Engineer: contrasts console-plus-sync with server.xml on disk. Senior: keeps secrets in server.env and wants XML in git. Staff: changes incident evidence to SHA versus sync generation. Principal: forbids unofficial Liberty cells and keeps Boot as greenfield.

topic: externalizing secrets off the WAS cell
question: jdbc/baypay on BayPayCell still uses J2C alias baypayDbAlias. How do you externalize secrets off the WAS cell for Liberty or Boot without putting BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in git or in a leftover cell document?
followUps: What is wrong with copying the J2C alias into a ConfigMap or a committed server.xml?
How does this map to Secrets Manager in us-west-2 or a Kubernetes Secret later?
expectedConcepts: J2C aliases are cell secrets
server.env / platform secret store / Secrets Manager
Never commit BAYPAY_DB_*
Rotate without a cell sync as the only path
engineerAnswer: I would stop storing the database password in baypayDbAlias as the target design. Liberty reads BAYPAY_DB_USER and BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD from server.env or the process environment. Boot does the same. Those values never go in server.xml, application-prod.yml, or a git ticket.
seniorAnswer: Externalizing means the process receives secrets at start from a store we can rotate. On a laptop that is a local env file that is gitignored. In baypay-prod it is a Secret or CSI. On ECS in us-west-2 it is Secrets Manager. I will not copy the J2C alias into a ConfigMap. I will not leave the cell alias as the production credential for the Liberty canary. Rotation is a new secret version plus a rolling restart, not a Morgan Hale console password change plus hope sync.
staffAnswer: Staff concern is blast radius and audit. A cell J2C alias is readable to anyone with cell admin. A dedicated secret for payment-service is grantable to one role. I want different credentials for refund and payment as soon as pools split. I will not apply NAT or EKS 'so we can use Secrets Manager' in a lab answer. Paper plus the store we already have is enough. I also refuse pasting the password into a chat with Priya to 'debug the DataSource.'
principalAnswer: Secrets leaving the cell is a control-plane decision: the cell is no longer allowed to be the vault. I will fund one pattern — env from a real secret store — across Liberty and Boot so we do not run three folklore paths. I will not accept 'the alias is fine until decommission' if wave 2 is already serving Avery Chen. Always-on vault appliances for a student lab are also a refuse; production gets a managed store in us-west-2.
commonMistakes: Putting BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in server.xml, a ConfigMap, or the admin-console screenshot in git
Reusing baypayDbAlias as the Liberty canary credential
Applying EKS or NAT so the interview answer can name Secrets Manager
scoreRubric: Engineer: moves BAYPAY_DB_* to env/server.env and out of XML. Senior: names rotation without cell sync and forbids ConfigMap passwords. Staff: splits credentials per app and refuses lab apply of EKS/NAT for secrets. Principal: makes the cell illegal as a vault and standardizes one store pattern.

topic: SSL handshake failure between plugin and member
question: On BayPayCell, ihs-east.baypay.example terminates Harbor Bike Co TLS, then the WAS plugin opens SSL to PaymentCluster member Pay2 and the handshake fails. How do you diagnose an SSL handshake failure between the plugin and a cluster member? Talk in symptom classes. Do not make a Kubernetes Secret common-name story the only answer.
followUps: What do you compare on ihs-east versus the Pay2 personal certificate and signer?
When is 'disable SSL to the member' an unacceptable workaround?
expectedConcepts: Plugin-to-member TLS is a second hop, not the merchant handshake
Trust, signer, hostname, and protocol mismatch as classes
Do not disable TLS
Not the kube TLS Secret CN lecture
engineerAnswer: Merchants can succeed to ihs-east and still fail on the plugin-to-member hop. I would look at IHS error logs and WAS SSL traces for handshake alerts, then compare the plugin's trusted signers to Pay2's personal cert. I would not turn SSL off to 'get payments through.'
seniorAnswer: Classes: expired or replaced member cert, missing signer on the plugin side, hostname mismatch against the transport host, protocol/cipher mismatch after a Java or IHS patch, or a plugin that still points at an old port. I compare plugin-cfg transports to the SSL repertoire on Pay2. I do not assume the merchant-facing IHS certificate is the same object. Stabilize is take Pay2 out of the plugin if other members handshake, not disable TLS on the cluster. A Kubernetes TLS Secret CN mismatch is a different estate and not this story.
staffAnswer: Staff method keeps two TLS stories separate: edge-to-merchant and plugin-to-JVM. Mixing them wastes the first hour. I want a cert inventory with not-after dates and who owns the trust store on ihs-east versus the node. I will not accept a jumphost HTTP 8080 success as proof merchants or the plugin are healthy. Rotation later needs overlap; a sudden replace without updating signers is how this class repeats.
principalAnswer: I will not run a payment platform where plugin-to-member TLS is folklore in a cell trust store. That is one reason the target front door is an ALB or Route with a declared certificate object. Until cutover I fund a dated inventory and I forbid 'disable SSL between IHS and WAS' as an emergency pattern. Interview answers that only recite a kube secret CN have studied the wrong hop.
commonMistakes: Disabling plugin-to-member SSL to restore traffic
Debugging only the merchant-facing IHS certificate
Lecturing a Kubernetes TLS Secret CN mismatch as the only handshake story
scoreRubric: Engineer: separates merchant TLS from plugin-to-member TLS and refuses to disable SSL. Senior: lists handshake symptom classes and drains the bad member. Staff: inventories two trust stores and rejects jump-box HTTP as customer proof. Principal: funds leaving cell folklore TLS and forbids emergency SSL-off.

topic: compatibility assessment that is honest about APIs
question: You are doing a WebSphere-to-Liberty compatibility assessment for payment.ear and refund.ear. What does an honest API assessment contain, and what must you refuse to call 'portable'?
followUps: How do you score SIBus, WS-* console bindings, PARENT_LAST, and javax versus jakarta?
Why must you not use the Spring Boot teaching app as proof the ears are ready?
expectedConcepts: Score contracts: packaging, JNDI, SIBus, WS-*, loaders, namespace
Cannot lift-and-shift list is required
Isolated JDBC names after rename
Boot proof is not ear proof
engineerAnswer: I would list what each ear looks up and which EE namespace it compiles. Servlets can move after jakarta and a war. jdbc/baypay must be renamed and isolated. BayPayBus, WS-* admin bindings, PARENT_LAST tricks, and javax EE 8 packages cannot lift-and-shift. The Boot fat JAR is a different packaging path.
seniorAnswer: Honest means a verdict per API: Liberty this quarter, Boot rewrite, or stay on ND until X. I will not mark JMS portable because a feature exists. I will not mark XA portable because jdbc/baypayXA appeared on some nodes. Refund can stay while a boring servlet refund moves — volume is why refund is wave 1, not 'simple APIs.' I write resource-refs I will change, not a slogan that 'Jakarta is compatible.'
staffAnswer: Staff assessment is a table other teams can challenge. Columns: URI, JNDI, messaging, WS endpoints, loader policy, EE namespace, verdict. I also fail it if every row says 'enable a feature.' Wave 0 has no traffic rollback, so a polite lie here becomes a production incident in wave 2.
principalAnswer: I use honesty as a risk control. I would rather keep an ear on BayPayCell for a quarter than ship a fake portable stamp. The assessment is how I decide whether Liberty is the ear path or whether we skip to Boot. I will not fund a program whose success metric is 'features enabled.'
