Using reference-apps/baypay as proof payment.ear is ready
A verdict of 'move everything this sprint' with no stay-on-ND rows
scoreRubric: Engineer: lists can-move vs cannot-lift-and-shift items by name. Senior: gives per-API verdicts and refuses feature-checkbox portability. Staff: publishes a challengeable table and separates Boot evidence from ears. Principal: accepts stay-on-ND as a valid quarter and funds honesty over speed.

topic: when not to leave WebSphere yet
question: A vendor slide says BayPay should leave WebSphere this quarter. When do you refuse to leave BayPayCell yet, and what do you still refuse to do while you stay?
followUps: Which dependencies make a stay cheaper than a dishonest Liberty canary?
What new work is still forbidden on the cell during a stay?
expectedConcepts: Stay when APIs cannot move safely
Stay is not a new ND investment
No new ears as greenfield
SLO and regulator evidence may force a hold
engineerAnswer: I would stay if payment.ear still needs SIBus, WS-* cell bindings, or javax APIs we have not migrated, and we cannot dual-run safely. Staying means we keep operating Pay1–Pay3. It does not mean we build a new cluster for a new product. Greenfield still goes to Boot.
seniorAnswer: I stay when rollback is a story, not a switch: no isolated pool, no idempotency store both estates share, or no edge rule to send /payment back. I also stay if the assessment is unfinished. A canary that is really an experiment on Avery Chen is not leaving; it is gambling. While we stay I still externalize what we can and I still refuse sticky sessions and shared jdbc/baypay growth.
staffAnswer: Staff stay criteria are written: open cannot-lift rows, missing SLO hold plan, regulator change window, or eventing we cannot drain. I will communicate stay as a dated decision with owners, not as loyalty to WAS. I will not use a stay to staff a bigger cell, hire more node agents, or put ND in Docker for 'cloud.' I will keep incident method on the cell sharp so the stay is operable.
principalAnswer: I refuse to leave when leaving is a slide. I also refuse to stay as a career for the cell. The principal job is to pick the cheaper honest risk: operate ND for a dated quarter, or move a thin war with a real rollback. I will not decommission under a sales deadline, and I will not open a second region of BayPayCell as DR. New value ships on Boot or a small Liberty process. The cell gets fixes, not features.
commonMistakes: Leaving this quarter because a slide said so, with no rollback or honest assessment
Using a stay as permission to build a new ND cell or ND-in-Docker
Shipping new products onto PaymentCluster while calling that modernization
scoreRubric: Engineer: names API blockers and still sends greenfield to Boot. Senior: stays when rollback or assessment is missing, and still stops smell growth. Staff: dates the stay with owners and keeps the cell operable, not larger. Principal: chooses honest risk, forbids cell DR/expansion, and puts new value off the cell.

topic: image layers and a fat vs layered JRE
question: Jordan Voss is packaging BayPay payment-service (Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5.5) as registry.baypay.example/baypay/payment-service:<tag>. Explain image layers and when you want a fat JAR on a slim JRE versus a more layered JRE/app split. Production must not depend on :latest.
followUps: Why is a full JDK in the final stage the wrong default?
Why is volume-mounting the fat JAR over the image a habit you refuse?
expectedConcepts: Layers cache; app layer changes more than the JRE
eclipse-temurin:21-jre in the final stage
Fat JAR is the teaching artifact; pin tags not :latest
Not ND in Docker
engineerAnswer: Each Dockerfile instruction is a layer. I want the JRE and OS layers stable and the application layer last so code changes rebuild little. Teaching image is eclipse-temurin:21-jre plus the Boot fat JAR on port 8080. I pin a digest or an immutable tag. I never ship :latest. I do not put dmgr-east in the image.
seniorAnswer: A fat JAR on a slim JRE is the honest default for this monolith: one artifact, one classpath, fast enough rebuilds. A layered Spring image or a jlink JRE can shrink pull time when the JAR changes often and the runtime does not. That is an optimization after the contract is right. A full JDK in the final stage is extra attack surface. Mounting a JAR over the image means we no longer know what is running. I rebuild when the base digest moves for CVEs, not by retagging :latest.
staffAnswer: Staff cares about rebuild provenance and pull cost in baypay-prod. I will pay for a layered build if Priya can show pull latency on three replicas, not because a blog likes layers. I want SBOM and pin of eclipse-temurin. I reject 'just use latest Temurin so we stay patched' without a digest bump pipeline. I also reject a fat traditional WAS profile layered 'like an app.' Containers package payment-service, not BayPayCell.
principalAnswer: Image shape is a supply-chain control. I standardize on a slim JRE, non-root, pinned tags, and an app layer we can rebuild in CI without a laptop daemon. I will fund layering when it is a pull-SLO problem. I will not fund a custom JRE project that delays leaving the cell. No live cluster is required to choose the Dockerfile.
commonMistakes: Shipping :latest or a full JDK in the final stage
Volume-mounting the fat JAR so the image is not the artifact
Containerizing dmgr-east or a traditional WAS profile
scoreRubric: Engineer: explains layers, slim JRE, fat JAR, and no :latest. Senior: treats extra layering as an optimization and refuses JDK/mount habits. Staff: ties layering to pull evidence and pinned base digests. Principal: standardizes supply-chain shape and will not delay the cell exit for a custom JRE.

topic: read-only root filesystem for a payment container
question: Sam Okada wants payment-service in baypay-prod to run with a read-only root filesystem. What must you still make writable for a Java 21 Spring Boot process, and what do you refuse to leave writable?
followUps: Where do you put tmp, logs, and the Hibernate or Tomcat scratch dirs?
Why is --privileged or writing the fat JAR at runtime a fail?
expectedConcepts: readOnlyRootFilesystem with explicit emptyDir mounts
Non-root UID
No secrets or JAR writes on the rootfs
Writable tmp only
engineerAnswer: I set the container read-only and mount emptyDir on the paths Java needs: /tmp and any logging or Tomcat work directory we actually use. The fat JAR and the JRE stay read-only. The process runs as a numeric non-root UID such as 10001. I do not write BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD onto the filesystem.
seniorAnswer: Read-only rootfs is a exploit-cost control. Spring Boot still needs temp space for uploads, Tomcat native scratch, or JVM attach files if we allow them. I declare those mounts. I do not discover them by watching CrashLoopBackOff. I refuse privileged, writable Docker.sock, and a writable / where a bad dependency can drop a binary. Logs go to stdout, not a growing file on the rootfs.
staffAnswer: Staff review checks the Pod spec: readOnlyRootFilesystem true, drop ALL caps, emptyDir for tmp, no hostPath. If Riley says 'the JVM cannot start,' we add the specific mount, we do not flip the rootfs back to writable. OpenShift SCCs may already forbid writable root; I align the Deployment rather than asking for a privileged SCC. Paper YAML is enough; I do not need a live cluster to review it.
principalAnswer: I make read-only rootfs part of the golden payment Pod, not an optional hardening ticket. Exceptions are named mounts with owners. A team that needs a writable root to unpack WAS has the wrong packaging. This control travels to Fargate as well: the task should not need a writable image layer.
commonMistakes: Leaving the root filesystem writable because 'Java needs tmp' without an emptyDir
Running privileged or as root so the process can write the JAR
Writing secrets or logs onto the container rootfs
scoreRubric: Engineer: sets read-only rootfs and names tmp mounts plus non-root. Senior: declares mounts up front and keeps logs on stdout. Staff: reviews SCC/caps/hostPath and will not revert the control. Principal: makes the pattern golden across kube and Fargate and rejects WAS-unpack images.

topic: requests/limits vs JVM heap and container OOM
question: In baypay-prod, payment-service has a memory limit and a Java 21 heap. How do requests, limits, and -Xmx relate, and why must you never set -Xmx equal to the container memory limit?
followUps: What does UseContainerSupport see, and what lives outside the heap?
What is the difference between a Java heap OutOfMemoryError and a kube OOMKilled?
expectedConcepts: requests place the Pod; memory limit is the cgroup
Heap is only part of RSS
Never -Xmx equal to the cgroup / Fargate memory
UseContainerSupport / MaxRAMPercentage with headroom
engineerAnswer: requests tell the scheduler how much to reserve. The memory limit is the cgroup. -Xmx is only the heap. Metaspace, stacks, code cache, and native buffers sit outside it. If I set -Xmx equal to the limit, the kernel can OOMKill the container while the heap still looks fine. I leave headroom. Teaching picture is like 1024m heap on a 2048Mi limit.
seniorAnswer: Java 21 UseContainerSupport sees the cgroup limit. MaxRAMPercentage can size the heap from that limit, but I still want explicit headroom I can explain. CPU limits throttle; memory limits kill (exit 137). I will not 'use all the memory' as a performance tip. A Java heap OOME is a JVM event. OOMKilled is a kernel event. I will ask for both artifacts before I change flags. The same rule applies on Fargate in us-west-2: never -Xmx equal to task memory.
staffAnswer: Staff sizing starts from in-flight work, then heap, then native, then limit. I reject PRs that set -Xmx to the limit to 'stop wasting RAM.' I also reject limit-less Pods in baypay-prod; that is noisy-neighbor risk, not generosity. If we are OOMKilled I will not first raise heap to the ceiling. I will ask what native consumer grew. No live cluster is required to refuse the forbidden pattern.
principalAnswer: Heap-equals-cgroup is a platform defect I will fail in review every time. It is in the same refuse list as ND-in-Docker. I want a published ratio for payment-service and I want it identical in kube YAML and ECS task memory. Capacity is replica count and pool size, not a bigger -Xmx jammed into the cgroup.
commonMistakes: Setting -Xmx equal to the container or Fargate memory limit
Treating a Java heap OOME and a kernel OOMKilled as the same event
Raising heap to 'use all the RAM' as a performance fix
scoreRubric: Engineer: explains requests vs limit vs heap and states the never-equal rule. Senior: distinguishes OOME vs OOMKilled and applies the rule on Fargate too. Staff: sizes from in-flight work and rejects limit-less or ceiling-heap PRs. Principal: standardizes the ratio and treats heap-equals-cgroup as a fail.

topic: liveness vs readiness for a slow-starting JVM
question: payment-service is Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.5.5 and is slow to class-load on a cold Pod in baypay-prod. How do you set liveness versus readiness (and startup) so Harbor Bike Co is not sent to a half-up JVM and so the kubelet does not restart a healthy boot?
followUps: Why must liveness not include a Postgres ping?
What path do you use instead of the aggregate /actuator/health?
expectedConcepts: startupProbe covers cold JVM
liveness is /actuator/health/liveness and restart-worthy only
readiness is /actuator/health/readiness and Endpoints
Do not live-probe the database
engineerAnswer: I point liveness at /actuator/health/liveness and readiness at /actuator/health/readiness on port 8080. I add a startup probe so the other probes stay off until the JVM has finished coming up. I do not use the aggregate /actuator/health for liveness. I do not need a live cluster to write those YAML fields.
seniorAnswer: A slow Boot process without startup will fail liveness during class-load and CrashLoop. That is a probe bug, not a bad image. Liveness must be cheap and lock-free. A database blip must not restart three replicas. That belongs on readiness, bounded. Readiness false removes the Pod from the Service so Avery Chen is not POSTed to a warming JVM. initialDelaySeconds alone is a weaker substitute; startup exists for this runtime.
staffAnswer: Staff review fails a chart that live-checks jdbc/baypay from liveness, or that uses / as the probe because 'ALB does that.' I want failureThreshold and timeout numbers that survive a GC pause without hiding a deadlock forever. I treat readiness 503 and CrashLoopBackOff as different classes. I will not bounce leftover dmgr-east because a Pod is not Ready.
principalAnswer: Probes are the payment admission contract. I standardize Actuator paths across kube and ECS health checks so we do not invent a third meaning of healthy. I will not accept a platform default that restarts JVMs on dependency blips. The spoken design does not require applying a cluster.
commonMistakes: Pointing liveness at Postgres or at aggregate /actuator/health
Omitting startupProbe so a cold JVM is killed
Using / or TCP as the only readiness signal for POST /api/v1/payments
scoreRubric: Engineer: maps the two Actuator paths and mentions startup. Senior: explains CrashLoop from early liveness and keeps DB off liveness. Staff: fails charts with / or JDBC liveness and splits symptom classes. Principal: standardizes health meaning across kube and ECS.

topic: CrashLoopBackOff from a bad Spring profile
question: The payment-service Deployment in baypay-prod is CrashLoopBackOff after Jordan Voss changed environment. How do you investigate a CrashLoop that might be a bad Spring profile? Stay on symptom classes; do not recite a lab's planted tag or port as the only story.
followUps: What log lines tell you the process never reached Tomcat on 8080 versus the kubelet killing it?
How do you stabilize without editing production by hand forever?
expectedConcepts: CrashLoopBackOff is a restart loop class
Wrong SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE / missing application-prod
Config versus image versus probe
Roll back the Deployment revision
engineerAnswer: CrashLoopBackOff means the container keeps exiting. I would read the previous Pod logs for a Spring failure to start — unknown profile, missing BAYPAY_DB_URL, or a failed DataSource on the prod profile. I would compare the env on the Pod to the profile the JAR actually contains. I would not delete the Deployment to 'clear it.'
seniorAnswer: Classes: process exits on bad config, liveness kills a slow start, OOMKilled, or a command that is wrong. A bad Spring profile is the first class if logs show the wrong application-*.yml or H2 defaults in prod. I check SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE, ConfigMap payment-config, and whether the image tag actually packaged application-prod. Stabilize is roll back to the last Ready revision or fix the env via the same pipeline. I do not kubectl edit forever. A debug tag or an unexpected listen port can be a member of this class; it is not the required answer.
staffAnswer: Staff method: previous logs, exit code, events, then the change list. I keep 'bad profile' unproven until the log names the active profiles. I will not bounce dmgr-east. I will not apply a new cluster to 'reset CrashLoop.' I communicate that Ready replica count is zero, so the Service has no Endpoints, so merchants fail at the front door. Remediation is a reviewed env change or a pin of the last good image.
principalAnswer: I want profiles to be boring: prod is explicit, default is fail-fast, and CI boots the JAR with the same env keys. A culture that debugs CrashLoop by shipping a special tag is a release-process bug. The platform should make the last-good revision one command, on paper or in Argo, without a live classroom cluster.
commonMistakes: Deleting the Deployment or bouncing leftover WAS to clear CrashLoopBackOff
Declaring a planted debug tag or port as the only correct story
kubectl-editing env in prod without a rollback path
scoreRubric: Engineer: reads previous logs and compares profile env to the JAR. Senior: ranks start-failure classes and rolls back a revision. Staff: keeps the profile hypothesis unproven and comms Endpoints=0. Principal: makes fail-fast prod profiles and last-good rollback the contract.

topic: OOMKilled with 'plenty of heap' left
question: Riley Okonkwo says the heap chart still had room when the payment-service Pod went OOMKilled. How can that happen, and what do you look at next? Do not set -Xmx equal to the limit as the fix.
followUps: Which native consumers are plausible on a Spring Boot payment JVM?
How would you change the limit versus the heap versus the code?
expectedConcepts: OOMKilled is cgroup RSS, not Java heap space
Direct memory, metaspace, threads, native libs
Never raise -Xmx to the limit
NMT / thread count / buffer leaks as classes
engineerAnswer: OOMKilled means the kernel hit the memory limit. Heap used is only part of RSS. Plenty of heap left is consistent with native growth: threads, metaspace, direct ByteBuffers, or a native library. I would not set -Xmx to the container limit. That makes the next kill more likely.
seniorAnswer: I ask for the limit, RSS, heap after GC, thread count, and whether NMT or a heap dump was taken after a non-prod reproduce. Classes: thread explosion from a connector or Hikari mis-size, direct memory, inflated metaspace from class generation, or a sidecar sharing the cgroup. Stabilize is add a replica or fail readiness on the dying Pod, then raise the limit only if native room was actually too small — while keeping heap below the new limit. I will not treat this as INCIDENT-1002's closed RCA; it is the same symptom class.
staffAnswer: Staff work is to stop the 'just give it more heap' reflex. I put heap, native, and limit on one diagram for Priya and Riley. I want a published headroom number for payment-service and a check in CI that rejects -Xmx equal to resources.limits.memory or Fargate memory. If dumps show a leak, we fix the leak. If they show legitimate native, we size the cgroup. Those are different tickets. No live cluster required; the exit 137 event plus heap chart is the teaching evidence shape.
principalAnswer: I will fail a platform that teaches engineers to fill the cgroup with heap. The payment JVM is a native process first. Capacity planning includes thread stacks and off-heap, then replica count. I will not accept OOMKilled-with-free-heap as a mystery more than once without NMT in the toolbox.
commonMistakes: Setting -Xmx equal to the memory limit because the heap looked empty
Treating OOMKilled as Java heap space
Raising heap as the first and only change
scoreRubric: Engineer: explains cgroup RSS vs heap and refuses heap-equals-limit. Senior: lists native classes and sizes limit with heap still below it. Staff: splits leak vs sizing tickets and adds a CI reject for the forbidden pattern. Principal: makes native-aware sizing a platform rule.

topic: OpenShift Route vs Ingress vs mesh
question: BayPay presents payments.apps.baypay.example in front of Service payment-service on 8080. Compare an OpenShift Route, a Kubernetes Ingress, and a service mesh. When is a mesh optional or the wrong next spend?
followUps: What job do Route and Ingress share that ClusterIP does not?
Why must you not treat Route and Ingress as different products that happen to share a hostname?
expectedConcepts: ClusterIP is east-west; Route/Ingress are L7 front doors
Route is the OpenShift overlay for the same job as Ingress
Mesh is optional; NetworkPolicy literacy first
Do not invent an employer mesh
engineerAnswer: The Service ClusterIP load-balances Pods on 8080. Ingress on Kubernetes and Route payment-route on OpenShift both terminate TLS and pick that Service for host payments.apps.baypay.example. A mesh is a sidecar or waypoint data plane for more east-west policy. We do not need one to expose payment-service.
seniorAnswer: I pick Ingress or Route based on the cluster we actually have, not on which YAML I memorized. Same host, same Service, same readiness. A mesh can add mTLS and retries. It can also add a second timeout story and another cert rotation. I will not install one to look modern. NetworkPolicy is the first blast-radius tool. IHS leftover on PaymentCluster is not an Ingress alternative.
staffAnswer: Staff decision is operational cost. If Sam already runs OpenShift, we use a Route and SCCs. If we are on generic kube, Ingress. If we are on ECS in us-west-2, this question becomes an ALB — we do not apply EKS just to have Ingress. I will not run Route and Ingress for the same host 'for HA.' I will not dual-home merchants to the cell plugin. Mesh is a platform product with an owner. Without that owner it is pager debt.
principalAnswer: Front-door API is one contract: TLS, host, Service, health. Route and Ingress are implementations. Mesh is a later control plane I buy only for a written east-west threat model. I refuse mesh as a substitute for leaving WebSphere, and I refuse EKS apply as the way to obtain Ingress. The spoken answer is paper architecture.
commonMistakes: Treating Route and Ingress as unrelated products or running both for HA
Installing a mesh to expose a ClusterIP Service
Applying EKS to get Ingress when ECS/Fargate or existing OpenShift already serves
scoreRubric: Engineer: maps Service vs Route/Ingress vs optional mesh. Senior: chooses the overlay you have and prefers NetworkPolicy first. Staff: will not dual-home or apply EKS for a front door you already have. Principal: one front-door contract; mesh only with an owner and a threat model.

topic: RBAC that lets a pipeline deploy BayPay only
question: Jordan Voss wants the CI pipeline to deploy payment-service in namespace baypay-prod and nowhere else. Design RBAC that lets that pipeline deploy BayPay only. What do you refuse to grant?
followUps: Why is cluster-admin on a deploy robot a fail even in a student cluster story?
How do Role versus ClusterRole and a dedicated ServiceAccount change blast radius?
expectedConcepts: ServiceAccount + Role + RoleBinding in baypay-prod
Least privilege on Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret
No cluster-admin, no other namespaces
Pipeline identity separate from human admins
engineerAnswer: I would create a ServiceAccount for the pipeline in baypay-prod and a Role that can get/patch/update the payment-service Deployment, Service, and maybe ConfigMap. I bind only that ServiceAccount in that namespace. I would not give cluster-admin. I would not let that account deploy into kube-system.
seniorAnswer: Least privilege is verbs and resources, not 'edit.' If the pipeline does not create Namespaces or ClusterRoles, those verbs stay off. Secrets: I prefer the pipeline not to get Secret contents if a controller injects them. If it must apply Secret objects, that is still namespace-scoped and audited. Human break-glass is a different account. I will not reuse Morgan Hale's leftover cell admin story as kube RBAC.
staffAnswer: Staff RBAC is a threat model: a stolen pipeline token should not read every Secret in the cluster or schedule to other teams' Projects. On OpenShift I use a Project and SCC that already constrain the SA. I review RoleBindings quarterly. I refuse a ClusterRole with * on * 'until we know the verbs.' Paper YAML is the review artifact; applying a live cluster is optional and not required to pass the design.
principalAnswer: Pipeline identity is part of the payment control plane. I will not sign cluster-admin bots. I want one SA per app or per team, admission that blocks privileged Pods, and a path to break-glass that is human and logged. This is the same least-privilege idea as an ECS task role that is nearly empty.
commonMistakes: Granting cluster-admin or *.* to the deploy robot
Binding a ClusterRole that can mutate every namespace
Reusing a human admin kubeconfig in CI
scoreRubric: Engineer: names SA + namespaced Role for payment-service. Senior: limits verbs and separates human break-glass. Staff: threat-models a stolen token and uses Project/SCC constraints. Principal: treats pipeline identity as payment control plane, aligned with empty task roles.

topic: platform golden path vs team-owned charts
question: Sam Okada offers a golden-path Helm chart for payment-service. Riley's team wants their own charts so they can 'move faster.' How do you decide platform golden path versus team-owned charts for BayPay?
followUps: Which knobs must stay golden (probes, heap-versus-limit, secrets, non-root)?
When is a team chart an acceptable exception with an expiry?
expectedConcepts: Golden path encodes probes, resources, identity
Team charts for app-specific env only
Exceptions are dated
Do not require a live cluster to decide
engineerAnswer: A golden path is a chart or template that already has port 8080, Actuator probes, non-root, read-only rootfs, and heap below the limit. The team should still own application env and the image tag. I would not copy the whole chart just to change one JVM flag.
seniorAnswer: I fork when the golden path cannot express a real need, and I upstream the need. I do not fork to disable readiness or to set -Xmx to the cgroup. Those PRs fail even in a team chart. Team-owned values for feature flags and replica count are fine. Team-owned security context is not.
staffAnswer: Staff looks at review load. Ten snowflake charts means Priya cannot tell which Pods violate the memory rule. I measure golden-path adoption, not chart count. I will provide an override file, not a fork, for SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE. OpenShift and generic kube should consume the same contract even if the front door object differs (Route vs Ingress).
principalAnswer: The golden path is how I scale a payment platform without hiring a platform engineer per squad. Teams own product config; the platform owns the pavement: identity, secrets, probes, resources, rollout hooks. I allow a dated exception for a migration wave, then I merge or I sunset. I will not accept team charts that recreate BayPayCell patterns — sticky sessions, writable root, kitchen-sink sidecars — as innovation.
commonMistakes: Forking the chart to disable probes or to set -Xmx equal to the limit
Forcing every team to invent RBAC, TLS, and resource math
Treating golden path as optional folklore with no review
scoreRubric: Engineer: splits golden pavement vs team env/tag. Senior: allows forks only for real gaps and still fails unsafe overrides. Staff: measures adoption and keeps Route/Ingress implementations behind one contract. Principal: dates exceptions and forbids cell-shaped snowflakes.

topic: rollout/rollback contract for payment APIs
question: Write the rollout and rollback contract for BayPay POST /api/v1/payments on Kubernetes or OpenShift. Harbor Bike Co retries. Idempotency-Key exists. What must be true before you call a revision good, and how do you undo?
followUps: How do maxUnavailable and readiness interact with in-flight authorizes?
What is different if the same contract is implemented as an ECS deployment in us-west-2?
expectedConcepts: Rolling update only after Ready
Rollback is previous revision, not a cell bounce
Idempotency across mixed versions
Canary then SLO, then 100%
engineerAnswer: A rolling update should only send traffic to Pods that pass readiness. I watch that the new image tag is on Ready replicas. Rollback is kubectl rollout undo or the GitOps revert to the last good tag — not a bounce of dmgr-east. Idempotency-Key must still work while two versions are up.
seniorAnswer: The contract is: canary a fraction, prove readiness and a synthetic POST, hold error rate and P99 against the teaching SLO, then continue. maxUnavailable stays low so we keep N+1 Ready capacity. I will not surge so hard that Hikari and the database are the rollout. Undo is the previous Deployment revision or ECS task definition in us-west-2 — same idea, different API. If mixed versions cannot honor the same Idempotency-Key, I stop the rollout. That is a compatibility fail, not a kube fail.
staffAnswer: Staff writes the gates: who watches RED, who can halt, how long we hold, and how merchants hear 'retry with the same key.' I will not call a revision good because the rollout object is Complete while readiness was a TCP probe. I keep a last-good pin in the change ticket. I refuse leftover IHS or BayPayCell as the rollback bunker. A wrong canary Service selector is a routing class I rehearse before the sale event, not during it.
principalAnswer: Rollout/rollback is a product SLA: time to halt, time to reverse, and data compatibility. I fund one contract that ECS, EKS, and OpenShift can all implement so the app team does not learn three cultures. I will not accept 'forward fix only' on authorize. I will not accept a hope DNS flip to a paper secondary as undo. No live cluster is required to write the contract.
commonMistakes: Calling the rollout done because replicas are STARTED/Running without Ready
Rolling back by bouncing dmgr-east or failing over to BayPayCell
Shipping a version that breaks Idempotency-Key during the mixed window
scoreRubric: Engineer: Ready-only traffic and undo to last tag, not the cell. Senior: canary plus SLO hold and mixed-version idempotency. Staff: names halt owners and refuses leftover IHS as bunker. Principal: one cross-platform contract with a time-to-reverse SLA.

topic: ConfigMap vs Secret vs CSI secret store
question: BayPay injects payment-config and database credentials into payment-service in baypay-prod. When do you use a ConfigMap, a Kubernetes Secret, and a CSI secret store? Where must BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD never live?
followUps: Why is a Secret still not a vault by itself?
How does this compare to ECS Secrets Manager injection in us-west-2?
expectedConcepts: ConfigMap is non-secret config
Secret is namespaced encoded credentials, not a vault
CSI/external store for rotation and least privilege
Never image, git, or ConfigMap for passwords
engineerAnswer: payment-config ConfigMap holds non-secret settings such as feature flags or log level. Secret baypay-db holds BAYPAY_DB_USER and BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD as env. Those values never go in the image, the Dockerfile, or git. A CSI driver can mount the same keys from a real store if the platform has one.
seniorAnswer: etcd Secrets are base64, namespaced, and readable to anyone with get secrets. That is better than a ConfigMap and not enough for a payment vault. I use CSI or an external store when we need rotation, audit, and IAM-style grant. On ECS in us-west-2 the analog is Secrets Manager plus the execution role. I still keep the env names identical: BAYPAY_DB_*. I do not invent BAYPAY_DB_PASS. I will not put the password in payment-config 'just for the lab.'
staffAnswer: Staff picks the store from blast radius. A stolen kubeconfig that can get secrets in baypay-prod is already a SEV. CSI plus short-lived mounts reduces lingering env copies. I will not apply EKS only to get CSI. If we are on OpenShift or Fargate, we use the store that platform already has. Rotation is a new version plus rolling restart. I document whether the process re-reads or only reads at start.
principalAnswer: I want one secret contract for the app: env names and rotation SLA. The backing store can be kube Secret, CSI, or Secrets Manager. I will not run three different key names across estates. I will not treat etcd as the long-term home for card-adjacent keys. Paper YAML plus ACCOUNT.md is enough to say that; applying CSI is not the interview.
commonMistakes: Putting BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in a ConfigMap, image layer, or git
Treating a Kubernetes Secret as a hardware vault
Applying EKS/CSI as the only acceptable answer when Fargate Secrets Manager already exists
scoreRubric: Engineer: splits ConfigMap vs Secret and forbids passwords in git/image. Senior: names Secret limits and maps to Secrets Manager. Staff: chooses store by blast radius and will not apply EKS just for CSI. Principal: one env contract; etcd is not the long-term payment vault.

topic: TLS certificate rotation without downtime
question: payments.apps.baypay.example needs a certificate rotation without downtime. How do you rotate TLS in front of payment-service? Give a method that works for Ingress, an OpenShift Route, or an ALB in us-west-2. Do not make a Kubernetes Secret common-name mismatch the only story.
followUps: What overlap must old and new certificates share?
What else besides the edge cert can break after a rotation?
expectedConcepts: Overlapping validity and dual-serve or atomic listener swap
Edge cert vs app trust store as separate classes
No downtime means no disable-TLS
CN/SAN is one class, not the only class
engineerAnswer: I install the new certificate before the old one expires and only then remove the old one. On Ingress or Route that is a new Secret or cert object, then the front door reloads. On an ALB in us-west-2 it is a listener certificate add-then-remove. I do not turn TLS off for the rotation window.
seniorAnswer: No-downtime means overlap: new cert is valid, hostname SAN still matches payments.apps.baypay.example, clients that cached the old chain still work until expiry. Classes if it fails: expired object, SAN/host mismatch, incomplete chain, front door still serving the old secret, or the app trust store not updated for a mutual-TLS hop. A kube Secret CN mistake is one member of the SAN/host class. It is not the only TLS story, and it is the wrong hop if we are talking about an ALB. I verify with a handshake to the public host, not with curl to Pod 8080.
staffAnswer: Staff rotation has an owner, a not-after page at seven days, and a ticket at thirty. I rehearse add-then-remove. I keep merchant TLS separate from plugin-to-member or mesh mTLS if those exist. I will not apply ACM in a student account as the interview proof. Paper dates plus the swap order are the answer. If rotation breaks only a canary, I halt the canary; I do not disable TLS platform-wide.
principalAnswer: Certificate rotation is a reliability feature I will staff. I want one hostname, a dated inventory, and a forbid on emergency TLS-off. I will not accept folklore trust stores on leftover IHS as the long-term path. The platform contract is overlapping certs and a handshake check that matches what Harbor Bike Co uses.
commonMistakes: Disabling TLS to rotate
Treating a Kubernetes Secret CN mismatch as the only possible TLS failure
Proving rotation with jump-box HTTP :8080 instead of the merchant hostname
scoreRubric: Engineer: add-then-remove overlap and no TLS-off. Senior: lists handshake classes and will not reduce them to one kube CN story. Staff: dates the inventory and keeps hops separate. Principal: staffs rotation as reliability and leaves leftover IHS trust folklore.

topic: service routing to the wrong canary
question: Jordan Voss launched a payment-service canary. Priya Nair says Harbor Bike Co traffic is hitting the wrong Pods. How do you diagnose Service routing to the wrong canary? Use selector and Endpoints classes, not a single memorized label RCA.
followUps: What do you compare among Deployment labels, Pod labels, and the Service selector?
How do you stabilize without deleting the production Service?
expectedConcepts: Service selector vs Pod labels vs Endpoints
Canary and stable must not share a selector by accident
Ingress/Route target Service is a second hop
Stabilize by selector or weight, not a cluster wipe
engineerAnswer: I would look at the Service selector and the Endpoints. If the canary Pods match the production Service labels, they will eat traffic. I would also check that the Route or Ingress points at the Service I think it does. I would not delete the production Service to 'reset routing.'
seniorAnswer: Classes: overlapping labels so both ReplicaSets land in one Endpoints list, a canary Service unused because the Route still targets production, a wrong weight, or a leftover selector from a copy-paste chart. I print labels on Pods and the selector on each Service. I do not guess from Deployment names. Stabilize is fix the selector or send the Route back to the stable Service. I keep production Endpoints non-empty while I do it.
staffAnswer: Staff method is three objects: front door, Service, Pods. I will not close on 'wrong canary' until Endpoints and a request id show which ReplicaSet served Avery Chen. I want canary labels in the golden path so this class is hard to recreate. I will not bounce leftover PaymentCluster. I will not apply a mesh to 'fix' a selector. Comms say whether merchants are on stable, mixed, or canary-only.
principalAnswer: Canary routing is part of the rollout contract. I will not allow two Deployments to share app=payment-service without a distinct track label and two Services. I fund that in the golden chart so Jordan cannot copy-paste this incident. Lucky 'it was the label' without Endpoints evidence does not max method.
commonMistakes: Deleting the production Service or the namespace to reset routing
Assuming Deployment name equals who receives traffic
Declaring one planted label typo as the only correct RCA
scoreRubric: Engineer: checks Service selector vs Endpoints. Senior: lists overlap/wrong-target classes and keeps prod Endpoints. Staff: requires request-id evidence and forbids mesh/cell as the fix. Principal: encodes track labels in the golden path.

topic: HPA on CPU vs SLO-based scaling for payments
question: Priya Nair proposes an HPA on CPU for payment-service. Harbor Bike Co load is bursty and the SLO is latency and success on POST /api/v1/payments. When is CPU autoscaling the wrong primary signal, and what would SLO-based scaling look like on paper?
followUps: What happens if you scale on CPU while the JVM is GC-bound or pool-bound?
How do you keep scale-up from exhausting jdbc/baypay or Hikari?
expectedConcepts: CPU HPA is literacy, not the payment SLO
Scale on in-flight, latency, or queue, with caps
Pool and DB headroom cap replicas
No live metrics-server required to reason
engineerAnswer: CPU HPA adds replicas when Pod CPU is high. A payment JVM can miss SLO while CPU is low if it is waiting on Hikari or the database. I would rather scale on something closer to the SLO, and I would cap replicas so we cannot stampede db-east. I can say that without a running metrics-server.
seniorAnswer: CPU is a useful ceiling signal and a bad sole signal. GC, lock wait, and pool wait do not always look like CPU. SLO-based scaling uses P99 or in-flight POSTs, with a max replica count derived from pool size and database connections. Scale-down is slow so we do not flap. I will not HPA on heap usage as a substitute for fixing a leak.
staffAnswer: Staff writes the cap first: max replicas times Hikari max must stay under the database budget. I will not enable HPA in production without that math and a load test on paper. On ECS in us-west-2 the same contract is service autoscaling on ALB request count or P99, not 'CPU because it is easy.' I refuse scale-to-zero for authorize.
principalAnswer: Autoscaling is an SLO feature with a budget, not a kube checkbox. I will fund custom metrics when CPU has already failed us, and I will not fund replica storms that DDoS our own ledger. HPA literacy is required; HPA-on-CPU-as-the-architecture is not.
commonMistakes: Using CPU as the only scale signal for a payment SLO
Unbounded HPA that exhausts the database pool
Requiring a live metrics-server to have an opinion
scoreRubric: Engineer: names CPU vs wait-bound SLO miss and wants a replica cap. Senior: proposes latency/in-flight signals and slow scale-down. Staff: does pool-times-replica math and applies it to ECS too. Principal: treats autoscaling as a budgeted SLO feature.

topic: when Kubernetes is optional for this workload
question: A principal interview asks whether BayPay payment-service must run on Kubernetes. When is Kubernetes optional for this workload, and what remains true on ECS/Fargate or OpenShift instead?
followUps: When would you stay on OpenShift you already have rather than applying EKS?
When is a single-process Liberty or even staying on ND for a dated quarter still the cheaper honest home?
expectedConcepts: ECS/Fargate is the student apply default
EKS/OpenShift are valid homes, not mandatory applies
App contract: 8080, probes, secrets, heap headroom
K8s optional when the platform you have already meets the contract
engineerAnswer: Kubernetes is one scheduler. The workload is still a Java 21 process on 8080 with Actuator probes and BAYPAY_DB_* from a secret store. On ECS Fargate in us-west-2 that contract is a task definition and an ALB. We do not have to apply EKS. If the company already has OpenShift, we use a Route instead of inventing a cluster.
seniorAnswer: I choose kube when we already operate it, or when we need its objects — Jobs, NetworkPolicy, many services — and we have owners. I choose Fargate when we want tasks without a cluster control plane, especially for a lab or a thin service. I choose stay-on-ND only as a dated source-estate hold, never as greenfield. I will not apply NAT plus EKS in a 90-minute lab to make the answer look cloud-native.
staffAnswer: Staff decision is operating cost and skills. A second control plane is an incident class. If Sam's team is OpenShift-strong, payment-service lives there. If the AWS landing is ECS-first, we do not create EKS 'for Kubernetes literacy in prod.' Literacy happens on paper and optional kind. Prod gets one home with a rollback contract. I still refuse ND-in-a-Pod as a compromise.
principalAnswer: Kubernetes is optional when it does not buy a control we will staff. I will sign ECS/Fargate, EKS, or OpenShift as valid homes. I will not sign 'apply EKS' as modernization. The non-optional pieces are the app contract, secret hygiene, heap-versus-cgroup, and a front door with health that matches Actuator. I will also say kube is the wrong spend while BayPayCell still has no honest exit plan — fix the assessment first. No live cluster is required for that decision.
commonMistakes: Treating EKS apply as the only correct home
Putting traditional WAS ND into a Pod to 'use Kubernetes'
Applying NAT/EKS in a lab so the interview can name kube objects
scoreRubric: Engineer: restates the app contract on Fargate vs kube. Senior: picks the platform you can operate and refuses lab EKS/NAT. Staff: avoids a second control plane and ND-in-a-Pod. Principal: signs multiple valid homes and will not buy kube as a slide.

topic: ECR scan findings you will block on
question: Jordan Voss pushes baypay/payment-service:<tag> to ECR in us-west-2 with scan-on-push. Which scan findings will you block a payment image on, and which will you ticket instead of stopping the train?
followUps: How do you treat a critical CVE in the JRE base versus a low finding in a test-only layer?
Why is :latest plus 'we will rescan tomorrow' not a control?
expectedConcepts: Scan-on-push in us-west-2, immutable tags
Block exploitable criticals on the runtime JRE/app
Ticket noise and unreachable findings with owners
No :latest
engineerAnswer: I block critical or high findings that sit in the runtime JRE or in a library payment-service actually loads. I ticket scanner noise and findings only in a discarded build stage. I will not promote :latest. I pin the tag that was scanned.
seniorAnswer: Block means the image does not become the ECS service or the baypay-prod Deployment. I care about exploitability on 8080 and about secrets accidentally left in a layer — that is a block even if the CVE score is low. A critical in an unused RPM I can remove by shrinking to eclipse-temurin:21-jre is a rebuild, not a waiver. I will not waive 'because the sale is tomorrow' without a dated exception and a rebuild plan.
staffAnswer: Staff policy is written: which severities, which packages, who may waive, how long. Priya and Sam share the waiver, not Jordan alone. I want scan findings attached to the tag in the change ticket. I will not apply extra AWS products to 'get a better scanner' for a lab. ECR scan-on-push in us-west-2 is enough to talk about the control.
principalAnswer: Supply chain is a payment control. I will stop a release for a reachable critical in Temurin or Spring. I will not stop the company for a noisy informational finding. I fund digest pins and rebuilds when the base moves. I refuse a culture of permanent waivers. The spoken policy does not require a live ECR apply.
commonMistakes: Shipping :latest or promoting an unscanned tag
Waiving a reachable JRE critical because a sale is tomorrow, with no date
Blocking the train on every informational finding with no policy
scoreRubric: Engineer: blocks runtime criticals and pins the scanned tag. Senior: includes secrets-in-layers and dated waivers. Staff: writes shared waiver policy without extra AWS apply. Principal: funds pin/rebuild and refuses permanent waivers.

topic: ECS Fargate task role vs execution role
question: On ECS Fargate in us-west-2, payment-service has an execution role and a task role. What does each one do, and what happens if you copy the execution role onto the task role 'to be safe'?
followUps: Who needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue for BAYPAY_DB_* at start?
What should the task role be if the JVM only talks JDBC?
expectedConcepts: Execution role: pull image, logs, fetch secrets at start
Task role: the JVM's AWS SDK identity
Least privilege; teaching task role near-empty
Do not attach AdministratorAccess
engineerAnswer: The execution role is for the ECS agent before my process exists: ECR pull in us-west-2, CloudWatch log streams, and GetSecretValue if secrets are injected at start. The task role is what the container assumes. Teaching payment-service only uses JDBC, so that role can be empty or near-empty. I do not copy the execution role onto the task role.
seniorAnswer: If I attach the execution role to the task, a compromised JVM can pull every image secret it could fetch and write logs as the agent. That is extra blast radius for no feature. If we later put receipts on S3, I add s3:PutObject on one prefix to the task role, not s3:*. KMS decrypt belongs with whoever actually unwraps the secret — usually the execution role at injection. AdministratorAccess 'so the lab works' is a fail.
staffAnswer: Staff review is two IAM policies with comments. I want the secret ARN scoped, not secretsmanager:*. I keep human deploy roles separate from both. A pipeline does not need the task role. I will not apply NAT or EKS to demonstrate IAM. Paper policies in us-west-2 are the artifact.
principalAnswer: Role split is the AWS version of pipeline SA versus app identity. I will fail a landing zone that merges them. I want the default task role empty so new AWS calls are explicit product decisions. That is how a payment platform stays least-privilege as features grow.
commonMistakes: Copying the execution role onto the task role or using AdministratorAccess
Putting GetSecretValue on the task role 'because the app might need it' when injection already happened
Scoping secretsmanager:* or s3:* for convenience
scoreRubric: Engineer: defines both roles and keeps the task role empty for JDBC. Senior: explains blast radius of a merge and scopes future S3. Staff: reviews ARN-scoped policies without extra apply. Principal: treats the split as a landing-zone control.

topic: ALB target unhealthy after a Java deploy
question: After a Java deploy, the ALB in us-west-2 marks payment-service Fargate targets unhealthy. Tasks show RUNNING. How do you work that symptom class? Do not treat a single memorized health-path RCA as the only correct story.
followUps: What must the ALB health check match on a Spring Boot 3.5.5 process?
What else besides path can make a RUNNING task fail the target group?
expectedConcepts: RUNNING is not healthy
Health check must match Actuator readiness, port 8080
Path, port, matcher, grace, security group as classes
Not Path=/ as the required answer
engineerAnswer: RUNNING means the task process was started. Unhealthy means the ALB health check is failing. I would compare the target-group path, port, and success codes to /actuator/health/readiness on 8080. I would also read the task logs to see if Spring finished starting. I would not bounce dmgr-east.
seniorAnswer: Classes: health path or port mismatch, matcher that does not accept 200 from Actuator, grace period shorter than a cold JVM, security group that blocks the ALB, or the app listening but readiness false. A check on / that 404s is one member of the path class — it is not the required interview RCA. Stabilize is keep the last healthy tasks in service if the service still has them, or roll back the task definition. I will not point the health check at /health or / unless we proved that path.
staffAnswer: Staff method: target health reason, security-group pair, task logs, change list. I keep each class unproven until quoted. I will not apply a new NAT or EKS to 'see targets better.' CloudWatch logs plus the target-group settings are enough. I communicate that merchants fail at the ALB while operators may still curl localhost 8080 on a jump path — that is not customer health.
principalAnswer: I standardize health on Actuator readiness across ALB, Ingress, and Route so this class shrinks. I will not accept a platform default of Path=/ for Java apps. I also will not grade interviews on reciting one lab's planted path. The contract is: the front door asks the same question kube readiness asks.
commonMistakes: Treating task RUNNING as healthy or bouncing leftover WAS
Declaring Path=/ as the only correct RCA
Proving health with jump-box HTTP while the ALB still fails merchants
scoreRubric: Engineer: separates RUNNING from ALB health and checks Actuator on 8080. Senior: lists path/port/matcher/grace/SG classes without requiring one planted path. Staff: quotes evidence and refuses extra apply. Principal: standardizes readiness as the front-door question.

topic: ECS vs EKS vs OpenShift for BayPay
question: Choose ECS on Fargate, EKS, or OpenShift for BayPay payment-service this quarter. The teaching apply default is ECS/Fargate in us-west-2. When does each win, and what do you refuse to apply just to have an opinion?
followUps: What skills and control-plane cost change the answer?
When is 'stay where we are' the staff answer?
expectedConcepts: Fargate default apply; EKS literacy
OpenShift valid if already operated
Stay is allowed
No NAT/EKS apply as the decision
engineerAnswer: If we are learning AWS with a thin Java service, I pick ECS Fargate in us-west-2: task definition, ALB, no cluster nodes. If the company already runs OpenShift, I keep a Route in baypay-prod. EKS wins when we already need Kubernetes APIs and we will staff the control plane. I do not apply EKS to decide.
seniorAnswer: I score owners, existing pavement, and how many services share the home. One payment process does not justify a new EKS estate. OpenShift brings SCCs and Routes we already taught. EKS brings upstream kube plus AWS IAM. Fargate brings less kube surface. I map the same app contract onto all three. I refuse ND-in-Docker as a fourth option.
staffAnswer: Staff writes ARCHITECT-1102 style: current skills, incident owners, secret store, front door, and cost of idle control plane. Stay on OpenShift is a first-class outcome. Stay on Fargate is too. I will not apply NAT Gateway or EKS 'for realism' in a lab or as the production answer when Fargate already serves. I will not run two front doors to the same merchants.
principalAnswer: I pick the home we will still operate at 3 a.m. I will sign any of the three. I will not sign a tourism cluster. The strategic fail is collecting platforms: cell plus OpenShift plus EKS plus Fargate for one URI. Modernization is leaving BayPayCell, not applying EKS.
commonMistakes: Applying EKS or NAT to make the choice look complete
Declaring Kubernetes the only correct home
Keeping BayPayCell as a fourth active front door
scoreRubric: Engineer: names Fargate default and when OpenShift/EKS win. Senior: scores owners and maps one app contract. Staff: allows stay and refuses NAT/EKS apply as the answer. Principal: refuses platform tourism and keeps leaving the cell as the goal.

topic: Secrets Manager + KMS envelope for payment keys
question: Design Secrets Manager plus KMS envelope encryption for BayPay payment keys and BAYPAY_DB_* in us-west-2. Who decrypts what, and what never appears in task-definition JSON in git?
followUps: When do you want a CMK versus the AWS-managed Secrets Manager key?
How is envelope encryption different from 'put the password in KMS'?
expectedConcepts: Secrets Manager holds the payload; KMS encrypts it
Execution role decrypts at injection
ARN in task def, never the secret string
Separate CMK for payment keys vs lab convenience
engineerAnswer: I store BAYPAY_DB_* in a Secrets Manager secret such as baypay/payment-service/db in us-west-2. The task definition references the ARN. Secrets Manager encrypts that payload with KMS. The execution role may kms:Decrypt and GetSecretValue at start. The password string is never in git.
seniorAnswer: Envelope encryption means KMS protects a data key, and that data key encrypts the secret bytes. I do not paste the password into KMS as if KMS were a file. A CMK lets me separate who may decrypt payment keys from who may decrypt a lab secret. Student apply may use the AWS-managed key and must say so. The task role stays off this path unless the JVM fetches at runtime, which teaching payment-service does not need.
staffAnswer: Staff splits DB credentials from any card-adjacent or signing keys: different secrets, different CMKs, different grants. Rotation is a new secret version and a rolling ECS deploy. I want CloudTrail on Decrypt. I will not create three extra CMKs in a 90-minute lab 'for realism,' and I will not apply NAT to reach Secrets Manager if the task already can. I refuse changeme in task-def JSON.
principalAnswer: Key hierarchy is a regulatory story I will keep boring: envelope with a CMK, scoped IAM, rotation SLA, no secret in git. I will not run a self-managed HSM in a student account, and I will not leave the cell J2C alias as a second vault. Payment keys do not share a decrypt grant with a shared platform sandbox.
commonMistakes: Committing the password in task-definition JSON
Treating KMS as a place to paste the raw password without Secrets Manager
One account-wide decrypt grant for every secret
scoreRubric: Engineer: ARN reference, SM plus KMS, execution role fetch. Senior: explains envelope vs file and when a CMK is worth it. Staff: splits key classes, rotation, and refuses lab CMK sprawl. Principal: boring hierarchy, no second cell vault, scoped grants.

topic: multi-account landing for a payment platform
question: Sketch a multi-account landing for the BayPay payment platform in us-west-2. What lives in which account, and what do you refuse to share with a student sandbox or a leftover cell admin?
followUps: Where do ECR, the ECS prod service, and logs go?
Why is a single account with AdministratorAccess not a landing zone?
expectedConcepts: Separate prod, nonprod, and shared services
us-west-2 as the teaching region
Least-privilege cross-account pull/deploy
No NAT/EKS required to draw the landing
engineerAnswer: I would keep a prod account for the ECS service and ALB, a nonprod account for student and QA, and maybe a shared account for ECR. Region is us-west-2. I would not put production BAYPAY_DB_* in the sandbox account. I can draw that without applying Organizations.
seniorAnswer: Shared services own the scanned ECR repo and maybe a log archive. Prod owns the Fargate service, prod secrets, and prod KMS. Nonprod can pull a promoted tag, not a floating :latest. Deploy roles are assumed from CI, not long-lived keys on laptops. I will not give Morgan Hale cell-admin equivalent in the prod AWS account.
staffAnswer: Staff landing includes SCPs that forbid leaving untagged ALBs and forbid creating NAT or EKS in the student OU. CloudTrail and GuardDuty-style audit live outside the app account. I will not put prod and sandbox in one account 'until we are bigger.' Blast radius is why we split early on paper. OpenShift-on-prem can still be a home; this landing is for the AWS slice, not a mandate to move everything.
principalAnswer: A payment landing zone is an OU design, not a VPC art project. I separate prod from playgrounds, I pin us-west-2, and I refuse always-on tourist control planes. I will not open us-east-1 as a hope DR in the same breath as the landing. DR is a dated plan, not a second account we forget to destroy. The cell is not an AWS account. I will not federate BayPayCell into the landing as 'hybrid HA.'
commonMistakes: One account, AdministratorAccess, prod secrets next to student labs
Applying NAT/EKS in every account to complete the diagram
Treating BayPayCell as a failover account
scoreRubric: Engineer: splits prod/nonprod/shared in us-west-2. Senior: scoped pull/deploy and no laptop long-lived keys. Staff: SCPs against tourist NAT/EKS and early blast-radius split. Principal: OU design, dated DR, cell is not hybrid HA.

topic: CloudWatch logs vs traces for a refund timeout
question: A Harbor Bike Co refund times out. Someone pastes a CloudWatch Logs Insights search from us-west-2 and calls it a trace. How do you use CloudWatch logs versus traces for a refund timeout, and what identifiers do you require?
followUps: When is a metric alarm enough, and when do you still need the refund.ear or refund-service log line?
Why is a leftover PaymentCluster PMI graph the wrong estate?
expectedConcepts: Logs are lines; Insights is a search, not a trace
correlationId / paymentId / traceparent
Traces need instrumentation and context propagation
CloudWatch is the AWS signal layer, not RCA by itself
engineerAnswer: I would search logs for the refund's paymentId or correlationId in the us-west-2 log group. That tells me which lines exist. A trace is a connected span tree if we actually instrumented and passed context. Insights is not that. I would not open dmgr-east PMI for a Fargate refund.
seniorAnswer: Timeout classes: client gave up, ALB idle timeout, app waited on JDBC, or a downstream refund path never answered. Logs show the last outcome line. Traces show where time was spent if spans exist. If there is no traceparent in the log, I will not invent a trace. I will ask for the next log line and the ALB access log. I keep refund-service and payment-service correlation ids aligned so a timeout can be followed without a cell dump.
staffAnswer: Staff method: evidence first. A CloudWatch alarm is a symptom. A search is a search. A trace is only a trace with spans. I will not apply X-Ray or OpenSearch in a lab to 'prove' the timeout. Paper logs plus optional trace files are enough. I refuse dual-writing leftover WAS logs into the Boot incident because both say refund.
principalAnswer: I fund correlation ids as the cheap contract and traces as a sampled product, not as a bill surprise. I will not accept Insights screenshots as RCA in an interview or an incident review. The platform must say which signal is authoritative for timeouts: log outcome versus span duration.
commonMistakes: Calling Logs Insights a trace
Bouncing leftover PaymentCluster for a Fargate refund timeout
Applying OpenSearch or X-Ray to manufacture evidence in a lab
scoreRubric: Engineer: searches by id and does not call Insights a trace. Senior: splits timeout classes and will not invent spans. Staff: keeps estates separate and refuses extra apply. Principal: funds ids first and forbids screenshot RCA.

topic: RDS failover vs application retry semantics
question: Sam Okada mentions Multi-AZ RDS failover in us-west-2 as a reason Harbor Bike Co saw payment errors. How should payment-service retry during a writer failover, and what must stay true for Idempotency-Key? This is literacy — you do not apply RDS.
followUps: What is unsafe about retrying a POST that already authorized?
Why is 'the database failed over' not proven RCA from a timeout alone?
expectedConcepts: Failover is a writer blip; retries must be idempotent
Do not blindly replay authorize
Pool recovery vs application semantics
No RDS apply in the student path
engineerAnswer: If the writer fails over, connections die and Hikari must reconnect. I would retry only operations that are safe, using the same Idempotency-Key for the merchant POST. I would not fire a second authorize to the card side without knowing the first outcome. I do not need to create RDS to say that.
seniorAnswer: Failover semantics: DNS or the driver moves to the new writer; in-flight transactions abort. The app sees connection errors, not a clean 200. Retries at the HTTP edge must not create duplicate money. Idempotency-Key plus a persisted intent is the control. A timeout alone does not prove failover. I want RDS events or an equivalent signal before I use that word. I will not bounce the ECS service as a substitute for pool reconnect, and I will not set -Xmx to task memory as 'capacity during failover.'
staffAnswer: Staff splits stabilize from story. Stabilize is fail readiness on tasks that cannot check out, keep last-good capacity, and tell merchants to retry the same key. The failover hypothesis stays unproven until we have a writer-change event. Lucky 'Multi-AZ' from a prior lab is not method. I will not apply multi-AZ RDS in a student account to rehearse this. Paper plus the retry contract is the bar.
principalAnswer: I treat database HA as a product that the application must be written for. Multi-AZ is not a cloak for non-idempotent POSTs. I will not buy RDS in every lab, and I will not fail the platform review if the retry story is missing even when Multi-AZ is on. DR to another region is a different conversation from failover in us-west-2.
commonMistakes: Blindly retrying authorize and creating duplicate money
Declaring RDS failover proven from a timeout or a prior lab
Applying multi-AZ RDS or bouncing the cell as the rehearsal
scoreRubric: Engineer: reconnects the pool and retries only with Idempotency-Key. Senior: needs a writer-change signal and refuses heap/cgroup 'capacity.' Staff: keeps the hypothesis unproven and will not apply RDS. Principal: makes idempotent POSTs the HA contract; region DR is separate.

topic: cost of NAT, ALB and idle Fargate
question: Priya Nair asks why last month's student AWS bill hurt. Talk through the cost of NAT Gateway, ALB, and idle Fargate for BayPay in us-west-2. What do you refuse to apply, and what do you destroy the same day?
followUps: Why is a public-subnet Fargate plus IGW the teaching apply, and what security trade-off must you say out loud?
What still costs money if the service desired count is zero?
expectedConcepts: ALB is dollars/day; Fargate is hourly; NAT is expensive
Do not apply NAT as the answer
Destroy ALB same day; tag Expiration
Empty ECR still has storage
engineerAnswer: ALB costs about dollars per day even with little traffic. Fargate costs while tasks run. NAT Gateway is an hourly plus data charge and is the usual bill shock. Student apply uses public subnets and an IGW instead of NAT. I destroy the ALB the same day. I do not apply NAT to make the VPC look 'real.'
seniorAnswer: Idle Fargate at desired count two still burns. Idle ALB burns more over a weekend. NAT burns whether the app is clever or not. I estimate before apply. If I cannot spend, I terraform validate on paper. Security trade-off of public Fargate: tasks are in public subnets with tight security groups, not a private-plus-NAT design. I say that out loud. ECR storage remains after I stop the service.
staffAnswer: Staff FinOps is tags Course=AEJE, Module, Lab, Environment=student, Expiration, plus a destroy checklist: ALB, service, cluster, images. I will fail a PR that adds NAT, EKS, or multi-AZ RDS 'for realism' in a 90-minute lab. I also fail leaving an ALB overnight. Prod is different: we pay for N+1 and an ALB on purpose, and we still do not pay for tourist NAT in every VPC.
principalAnswer: I treat NAT as a product we buy when private subnets are required and someone owns the bill — not as a default. Labs refuse it. Prod may still refuse it if public-plus-SG is the signed design. I will not let idle ALBs become shadow production. Expiration tags are a control, not decoration.
commonMistakes: Applying NAT Gateway or EKS so the lab looks production-like
